papers.title: Modeling extreme mass-ratio inspirals in astrophysical and dark-matter environments
papers.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals offer a powerful probe of massive black holes and their environments, but interpreting their signals requires accurate models of orbital dynamics and radiation. Here we bring together advances in black-hole perturbation theory to establish a unified relativistic framework for adiabatic inspirals in perturbative astrophysical environments. Built on the modified Teukolsky formalism, the framework requires neither post-Newtonian nor slow-rotation approximations. As a first application, we calculate the leading cloud-induced corrections to gravitational-wave fluxes and conservative orbital dynamics for circular, equatorial inspirals around a rotating black hole surrounded by a synchronized ultralight scalar cloud, combining these corrections with the previously calculated scalar response. In our fiducial system, a cloud containing $10^{-4}$ of the black-hole mass produces about $-57.3$ radians of orbital dephasing over two years. The phase contributions from gravitational-wave flux corrections and background-induced orbital shifts each exceed the scalar contribution in magnitude and partially cancel, highlighting the need for coupled matter-gravity modeling. Extensible to other environments and modified gravity theories, our framework provides the relativistic inputs needed to assess detection losses and parameter biases, and to probe the nature of black-hole environments with future space-based gravitational-wave observations.

ai_review.summary: This paper develops a relativistic framework for environmental corrections to adiabatic EMRIs using the modified Teukolsky formalism, without a post-Newtonian or slow-rotation expansion. Its worked example is a circular, equatorial inspiral around a rotating black hole with a synchronized ultralight scalar cloud. The calculation combines changes to gravitational radiation, conservative orbital dynamics and the scalar response. For the fiducial cloud mass of 0.01% of the black-hole mass, it reports approximately -57.3 radians of orbital dephasing over two years. The gravitational and conservative contributions exceed the scalar contribution individually and partially cancel. The main contribution is a coupled calculation showing why scalar-flux-only estimates can miss the leading environmental effect; it is not yet a detector-level parameter-bias forecast.

papers.title: Modified Teukolsky Formalism for Extreme Mass-Ratio Inspirals in Higher-Derivative Gravity
papers.abstract: In this work, we study a model problem involving a point particle spiraling into a non-rotating black hole in higher-derivative theories of gravity. In such theories, both the background spacetime and the generation and propagation of gravitational waves differ from those in General Relativity. We develop a modified Teukolsky formalism to describe gravitational waves sourced by the point particle and, as an illustrative example, compute the resulting fluxes to the black hole horizon and null infinity for a cubic gravity theory. The formalism is constructed in a way that can be naturally extended to rotating black holes. These results represent essential steps to build extreme mass-ratio-inspiral waveforms in modified gravity theories, which may also be rescaled to approximate waveforms from comparable-mass binary black hole systems, analogous to existing approaches in General Relativity.

ai_review.summary: The authors construct modified Teukolsky equations for radiation from a point particle orbiting a nonrotating black hole in higher-derivative gravity. A parity-preserving cubic-curvature theory supplies the worked example, including corrections to energy fluxes through the horizon and at infinity. These corrections have opposite signs and partly cancel in the total flux; the horizon correction is comparatively large relative to its GR counterpart. The text reports multipolar convergence, a weak-field comparison with an independent post-Newtonian prediction, and checks using field-redefined descriptions. This supplies a concrete radiation calculation for future EMRI waveform models. It does not yet include the secondary's tidal response, which the authors identify as entering at the same perturbative order, or provide a complete rotating inspiral waveform.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Central to Teukolsky methods, EMRIs, horizon fluxes and tidal-response modeling; particularly useful alongside the environmental-EMRI paper.
ai_review.quality_reason: Independent post-Newtonian limits, multipolar convergence and field-redefinition checks give complementary support to the source construction and flux calculation. The omitted secondary tidal term is explicitly acknowledged.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: flux results, conclusion and validation appendices. Figures and algebra were not independently checked. The worked model is nonrotating and point-particle based; the secondary's finite-size response remains necessary for complete waveforms.

ai_review.evidence_quote: provide complementary checks of the modified Teukolsky construction

papers.title: Periodic orbits and gravitational-wave emission from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals around rotating charged black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract: Within general-relativistic descriptions, the no-hair theorem dictates that black-hole geometries possess just three intrinsic physical quantities: mass, angular momentum, and electric charge. Black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) are equivalent to those composed of anisotropic matter and can develop "hair" structures near the event horizon, serving as ideal testbeds for modified theories of gravity. Working within Einsteinian gravitational theory, we adopt a coupling construction between gravity and NED matter, focusing explicitly on the Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg (EEH) variant with the power-index parameter fixed at s = 2. In this framework, a rotating, charged NED black hole extends the Kerr-Newman geometry with extra correction terms. Treating spin a and NED charge q as primary control variables, we examine test-particle dynamics inside extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) configurations. We derive equatorial timelike geodesics and the effective potential. Through numerical evaluation of marginally-bound orbits (MBO) and innermost stable circular orbits (ISCO), we explore how these parameters reshape the energy-angular-momentum (E-L) phase-space. Using the (z, w, v) integer-valued orbit taxonomy, we compute the two gravitational-wave polarization modes h+ and hx via the adiabatic approximation and quadrupole radiation prescription. Larger values for a and q drive inward contraction for bound trajectories while displacing the E-L phase-space toward smaller angular-momentum values. Periodic-orbit zoom-whirl signatures grow increasingly prominent, while larger parameter values shorten the waveform periods and enhance signal amplitudes. Our results provide theoretical support for space-borne gravitational-wave observatories including LISA and TianQin, enabling prospects for discriminating NED black-hole spacetimes and performing observational checks on the no-hair theorem.

ai_review.summary: This study explores equatorial test-particle motion around a rotating charged black hole in an Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg nonlinear-electrodynamics model. It derives an effective radial potential, computes marginally bound and innermost stable circular orbits, and classifies periodic zoom-whirl trajectories using the usual integer orbit taxonomy. Varying spin and charge changes the allowed energy-angular-momentum domain, orbital geometry and the resulting pulse structure. Gravitational-wave polarizations are generated with an adiabatic quadrupole kludge rather than a sourced black-hole perturbation calculation. The work is most useful as an illustrative catalog of orbital and waveform behavior in a particular non-Kerr geometry. Its suggested applications to no-hair tests require more accurate radiation modeling and an inference analysis before differences between plotted signals can become quantitative observational claims.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Connects EMRIs, periodic resonances and waveforms, but the specific charged nonlinear-electrodynamics model is less central than generic perturbation or environmental methods.
ai_review.quality_reason: The effective-potential analysis, orbit tables and Kerr-limit check make the model calculation traceable. The quadrupole kludge supports exploratory waveform comparisons more directly than precision observational tests.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, waveform description and conclusion. No independent metric, orbit or waveform verification. Results concern equatorial test-particle orbits in one charged model; detector discrimination is not established by waveform differences alone.
ai_review.evidence_quote: When q=0 , the model strictly degenerates into Kerr spacetime

papers.title: Chaotic Imprints in Gravitational Waves from Extreme-Mass-Ratio-Inspirals Embedded in Dark Matter Halo
papers.abstract: We investigate imprints of chaos in gravitational waves from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals configuration, where a stellar massive object, confined in an external potential as a harmonic oscillators, orbits a supermassive Schwarzschild-like black hole embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter halo. In our previous work (Das S, et al., Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals embedded in dark matter halo: Existence of homoclinic orbit and horizon-induced chaos, Sci. China-Phys. Mech. Astron. 69, 290413 (2026)), we demonstrated the system's transition from non-chaotic to chaotic dynamics by analyzing Poincaré sections, orbital evolution, and Lyapunov exponents across different energies and dark matter halo parameters. In this work, we compute the gravitational waveforms of the small celestial object along different chaotic and non-chaotic orbits by implementing the numerical kludge scheme. We further perform spectral analysis of the gravitational waveforms from such orbits. In particular, we show that when the system is in a chaotic state, the gravitational wave signals are characterized by broader frequency spectra with finite widths, irregular waveform modulations with comparatively large strain excursions for the chaotic trajectories considered here, together with modified energy-emission characteristics, distinctly differentiating them from the signals generated during the system's non-chaotic state. Furthermore, we discuss the potential detectability of these orbits for upcoming observatories like Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), TianQin, and Taiji, emphasizing the significant potential for detecting chaotic imprints in gravitational waves to substantially enhance our understanding of chaotic dynamics in black hole physics and the dark matter environments of galactic nuclei.

ai_review.summary: The paper studies gravitational-wave signatures of regular and chaotic trajectories in a Schwarzschild-like black-hole spacetime with a Dehnen dark-matter halo and an imposed harmonic confining potential. Building on earlier orbital chaos diagnostics, it generates numerical-kludge waveforms and examines their frequency spectra and recurrence structure. Chaotic examples show less periodic signals, broader spectral content and irregular strain excursions. The authors explicitly note that absolute amplitude depends on the chosen trajectory and is not a monotonic measure of chaos. Characteristic strains are compared with proposed space-detector sensitivities. The result is a conditional demonstration of waveform signatures within this forced dynamical model, rather than evidence that a dark-matter halo alone produces comparable chaos in a self-consistently evolving astrophysical inspiral.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Relevant to environmental EMRIs and nonintegrable orbital dynamics, with possible connections to resonance studies. The externally confined model limits direct transfer to realistic inspirals.
ai_review.quality_reason: Spectral and recurrence analyses provide multiple diagnostics within the toy system. Astrophysical and detectability claims carry greater uncertainty because of imposed confinement, short trajectories and neglected radiation reaction.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and discussion/conclusion. No independent numerical or figure check. Harmonic confinement is imposed, radiation reaction is neglected, radiation is quadrupolar and the detector comparison omits galactic confusion noise.
ai_review.evidence_quote: the absolute strain amplitude is trajectory dependent and is not, by itself, a monotonic diagnostic of chaoticity

papers.title: Conservative Orbital Resonance Networks as Local Environmental Diagnostics for Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals
papers.abstract: LLow order orbital resonances provide localized probes of the conservative geometry sampled by extreme mass ratio inspirals. We study fixed eccentricity and inclination slices of the ordered $3{:}2$, $5{:}3$, and $2{:}1$ polar to radial resonance surfaces in source consistent anisotropic black hole environments, treating rotation strictly to first order. A horizon regularized Dehnen sequence produces unequal resonance displacements, reaching $-7.17\%$, $-5.45\%$, and $-3.94\%$ in a fixed global benchmark. After matching both the total environmental mass and the enclosed mass at $10M_\bullet$, we compare Dehnen and Einasto inspired families. Two dimensionless network spacing ratios are organized primarily by the local logarithmic enclosed mass slope: for the common $β=2$ regularization their maximum cross family departure from a shared linear relation is $4.1\times10^{-4}$, while varying the horizon taper through $β=2$--$4$ increases the departure to at most $2.1\times10^{-3}$. The unequal ordering of the three resonance displacements holds at every point of a directly evaluated finite eccentricity and inclination grid. A six observable conservative response analysis is numerically full rank but strongly ill conditioned and nearly aligned with orbital nuisance directions. The result therefore establishes local conservative profile sensitivity, not unique tomography or a detector level parameter recovery forecast.

ai_review.summary: This paper asks whether several conservative orbital resonances can reveal local structure in a black-hole environment. It compares fixed-eccentricity and fixed-inclination slices of the 3:2, 5:3 and 2:1 polar-to-radial resonance surfaces, treating rotation only to first order. Matching environmental mass measures between Dehnen and Einasto-inspired profiles leaves unequal resonance shifts and spacing ratios correlated with a local enclosed-mass slope. Numerical convergence tests, analytic limits and a weak-environment check support these conservative calculations. A response analysis also finds strong degeneracy with orbital nuisance directions. The contribution is therefore a carefully bounded local diagnostic, rather than unique environmental tomography. Predicting measured resonance timing or detector constraints would additionally require radiation transport, phase-dependent resonance jumps and environmental dissipation.
ai_review.relevance_reason: An especially close match to EMRIs, resonances and environmental effects, with explicit links to missing self-force inputs for dissipative extensions.
ai_review.quality_reason: Matched-profile comparisons, numerical refinement and analytic-limit checks support a narrowly stated result. The authors distinguish internal numerical accuracy from physical modeling errors and explicitly expose inference degeneracies.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, numerical checks and conclusion. No independent code or figure verification. Rotation is first order; self-force resonance jumps and environmental drag are absent, and the effective matter model is not globally physical near the horizon.

papers.title: Biases in Ringdown Tests of General Relativity from Gravitational-Wave Microlensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) ringdown signals provide a powerful probe of the strong-field regime of general relativity (GR) through black hole spectroscopy and tests of the Kerr hypothesis. However, unmodeled propagation effects can bias the inference of remnant properties and the interpretation of ringdown features. We investigate the impact of gravitational lensing on ringdown inference and tests of GR using GW150914-like simulated signals spanning the long-wavelength, wave-optics, and geometric-optics regimes. We perform complementary time-domain post-merger and frequency-domain full inspiral--merger--ringdown analyses using unlensed waveform models. We find that lensing in the wave-optics regime can produce substantial biases in the inferred remnant mass and spin and can strongly affect the inferred modal content of the ringdown. In particular, it can spuriously favor the presence of the first overtone, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{221}_{220}\sim40$, even though the injected signal has no support for it. Parameterized ringdown tests can likewise yield strong apparent support for deviations from the Kerr quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{\rm modGR}_{\rm GR}\sim8$. In contrast, the evidence for higher-order modes remains largely unchanged for the simulated signals considered here. The parameterized analysis using the entire signal further shows that microlensing can bias the inferred frequency of the dominant $(2,2,0)$ QNM. These results demonstrate that unmodeled microlensing can produce systematic biases and spurious signatures in ringdown analyses, potentially affecting precision tests of the Kerr hypothesis.

ai_review.summary: This study tests whether gravitational microlensing can masquerade as unexpected ringdown physics. It lenses GW150914-like simulated signals with an isolated point-mass lens, then analyzes them using unlensed post-merger and full inspiral-merger-ringdown models. Wave-optics interference can bias inferred remnant properties and produce spurious support for an overtone or deviations from Kerr quasinormal-mode frequencies. By contrast, a large waveform mismatch in the geometric-optics regime does not necessarily imply a large frequency or remnant-parameter bias. Agreement across complementary analysis methods strengthens the warning that propagation effects can contaminate source-based tests. The numerical evidence is a controlled demonstration using zero-noise injections and restricted source and lens configurations, not a forecast of how often such false deviations occur in detector data.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Directly links gravitational lensing, quasinormal modes and gravitational-wave tests of black-hole perturbation theory.
ai_review.quality_reason: Complementary Bayesian post-merger and full-signal analyses probe distinct failure modes and distinguish mismatch from parameter bias. Controlled injection assumptions are clearly stated and bound the interpretation.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract and conclusion. Bayesian computations and figures were not reproduced. The study uses GW150914-like sources, a point-mass lens and zero detector noise; quoted evidence ratios should not be generalized to populations.

papers.title: Detectability of Gravitational Waves from Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals on Periodic Orbits around Bardeen Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate gravitational wave (GW) signatures from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) around a Bardeen black hole, modeling the small object as a test particle, and provide a framework for probing strong-field spacetime geometry. We first present the equations of motion for test particles around a Bardeen black hole and characterize circular orbits in the parameter space of energy and angular momentum. Using Levin's classification, we adopt the extended classification scheme to classify periodic orbits around a Bardeen black hole. We then compute GW waveforms in both the time and frequency domains, as well as the corresponding characteristic strains, for these periodic orbits and compare them with the sensitivity curves of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), the evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (eLISA), the TianQin mission, the Big Bang Observer (BBO), and the Decihertz Interferometer Gravitational wave Observatory (DECIGO). We find that detectability is controlled primarily by the luminosity distance. At a luminosity distance of 200 Mpc, the signals can exceed the sensitivity curves of BBO and DECIGO and are comparable to the LISA sensitivity curve, whereas at 2 Gpc, they remain below the sensitivity curves of all detectors considered. These results suggest that EMRIs on periodic orbits around Bardeen black holes offer a promising avenue to probe strong-field gravity and the properties of Bardeen black holes.

ai_review.summary: The authors construct periodic geodesics around a nonrotating Bardeen black hole, using eccentricity, a latus-rectum parameter and an integer orbit classification. An analytic parametrization helps choose orbital constants, after which a simplified numerical-kludge prescription produces time-domain polarizations and frequency-domain characteristic strains. The study varies orbital families, viewing geometry, central mass and source distance, then compares example strains with proposed space-based detector sensitivity curves. Sources at 200 Mpc can approach or exceed selected sensitivity curves, whereas examples at 2 Gpc are weaker. This is useful as an exploratory periodic-orbit signal study in a regular-black-hole model. It does not yet establish an evolving EMRI waveform, a robust detection horizon or the ability to distinguish Bardeen geometry from competing models.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Touches EMRIs and periodic orbital structure, but its regular-black-hole examples and simplified radiation model are less central to precision self-force and Teukolsky work.
ai_review.quality_reason: The orbit parametrization is useful, but simplified kludge signals and sensitivity-curve overlays provide limited support for the broader observational claims. Precision detectability needs stronger waveform and inference evidence.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, waveform prescription and conclusion. No independent validation of formulas or figures. Spin, radiation reaction and environments are omitted; a strain-curve comparison alone is not a detection or discrimination calculation.
ai_review.evidence_quote: neglecting the effects of black hole spin, radiation reaction, and astrophysical environments.

papers.title: Searching for lensed gravitational waves with unlensed templates
papers.abstract: Gravitational lensing can split the signal of a binary merger into two images, which either overlap and interfere or arrive as separate events. We show that the matched-filter output of every two-image template can be straightforwardly constructed from the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) time series that searches already compute with unlensed templates. This enables a marginalized detection statistic that increases search sensitivity without additional matched filtering and is more than 150 times faster than an explicit lensed template bank. For overlapping images in the geometric-optics regime, our two-image method recovers $\gtrsim97\%$ of the optimal SNR from point-mass and singular isothermal lenses, compared with as little as $67\%$ captured by unlensed templates, with substantial gains also for Chang-Refsdal and cored isothermal lenses. Overlapping lensed signals moreover fail the signal-consistency test that is used to down-rank noise transients. Our two-image method restores the consistency and increases the sensitive volume by roughly $2$-$4\times$ for the strongly down-ranked signals. For separated images, our method enables an efficient coherent search for pairs in which neither image is significant alone. Near fold caustics, this increases the sensitive volume by factors of 1.8-2.6 over requiring two independent detections, and up to 1.6 over a targeted counterpart search. Our method is applicable to any matched-filtering search.

ai_review.summary: This paper shows how matched-filter outputs for two-image lensed gravitational-wave templates can be assembled from the complex SNR series already computed with unlensed templates. The construction avoids an additional matched-filter operation for every lens configuration and supports a marginalized search statistic. Tests examine overlapping images, signal-consistency penalties and separated pairs whose individual images may be subthreshold. In the studied regimes, the method recovers otherwise lost SNR and improves sensitive volume after accounting for search thresholds. Gaussian-noise experiments and explicit discussions of trial factors make the performance argument more useful than a waveform-overlap comparison alone. The demonstration nevertheless uses a single detector and a restricted injection setup; extension to real data, detector networks and more complicated image structures remains future work.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Strong match to gravitational lensing and gravitational-wave methods, with a concrete computational technique that could inform lensing searches and waveform-systematics studies.
ai_review.quality_reason: The analytic reuse of existing SNR series is backed by controlled signal/noise experiments, explicit threshold accounting and reported reproducibility materials. Single-detector Gaussian-noise tests appropriately limit the performance claim.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, conclusion and consistency-test appendix. Code and figures were not independently checked. Results use a restricted binary example and Gaussian noise; real network backgrounds and lenses with more images require additional validation.

ai_review.evidence_quote: We used a single detector with stationary Gaussian noise

papers.title: Probing parity-breaking black-hole geometry with extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational-wave signatures of equatorial reflection symmetry breaking in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) around a parity-violating conformal Kerr black hole. For the circular-orbit branch connected to equatorial Kerr orbits, we derive the dynamics through second order in the dimensionless deformation parameter $\varepsilon$ and construct adiabatic inspirals and gravitational-wave signals using a mass-quadrupole prescription. Equatorial reflection maps $\varepsilon$ to $-\varepsilon$, making the polar displacement odd and the orbital frequency and energy even in the deformation. The induced first harmonic has a small direct contribution for the configurations studied, while second-order dynamical corrections accumulate over many cycles to produce appreciable dephasing. We find that rapid black-hole rotation enhances these phase effects and the associated noise-weighted waveform mismatch. For a one-year inspiral of a $10M_\odot$ object into a $10^6M_\odot$ black hole with $a/M=0.9$ and viewing inclination $ι=2π/3$, the fixed-parameter mismatch reaches the comparison benchmark $\mathcal M=0.01$ at approximately $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$, without optimization over time, phase, or Kerr parameters. A single-parameter Fisher analysis also indicates improved local sensitivity to $\varepsilon$ at high spin. These results connect the reflection properties of the circular branch to accumulated source-phase effects and complement tests of propagation birefringence. The sensitivity estimates remain conditional on the adiabatic quadrupole model and the adopted comparison procedure; robust observational constraints require more accurate radiation modeling and a full parameter-estimation analysis.

ai_review.summary: This paper examines EMRI signatures of equatorial reflection-symmetry breaking in a parity-violating conformal Kerr geometry. It follows the circular branch connected to equatorial Kerr orbits and keeps deformation corrections through second order. Reflection symmetry makes the polar displacement odd in the deformation, while orbital frequency and energy are even. In an adiabatic mass-quadrupole model, accumulated dynamical phase corrections can matter more than the additional first harmonic, particularly at high spin. Fixed-parameter mismatches and a conditional single-parameter Fisher calculation illustrate possible sensitivity. The useful contribution is the connection between symmetry, orbital perturbation orders and cumulative phase effects. The quoted mismatch benchmarks are not parameter bounds: time, phase and Kerr parameters are not optimized, and full inference and numerical-error checks remain necessary.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Relevant to EMRI dynamics and perturbative waveform systematics; the symmetry argument is potentially more transferable than the particular parity-breaking metric forecast.
ai_review.quality_reason: A symmetry-organized perturbative calculation clarifies which effects can accumulate. The quantitative forecasts remain conditional on quadrupole radiation, fixed-parameter comparisons and incomplete treatment of parameter correlations.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, conclusion and sampling discussion. No independent calculation or figure verification. Restricted circular orbits, quadrupole fluxes and conditional Fisher widths do not establish robust observational constraints.
ai_review.evidence_quote: does not optimize relative time or phase

papers.title: Moving Beyond Quasinormal Modes and Reinterpreting Direct Waves in Binary Black Hole Merger-Ringdowns
papers.abstract: Based on black-hole perturbation-theory calculations and an effective-one-body picture of binary black hole mergers, it has been suggested that a direct wave may be present and measurable in the ringdown. Furthermore, it has been suggested that this signal might originate from substantially inside the light ring (or photon sphere) of the remnant black hole, perhaps even from close to the event horizon. In this paper, we present three independent strands of evidence against such claims. In the process, we show that there is indeed an early-time part of the ringdown signal that cannot be directly modeled by quasinormal modes. However, there is no evidence that this is a direct wave as it has previously been defined, and we show that the properties of this component are related to the remnant's light ring rather than its horizon.

ai_review.summary: The paper reassesses an early merger-ringdown component that cannot be represented directly by quasinormal modes. It argues against identifying this component with radiation emitted near the event horizon during a plunge. Three complementary lines of evidence instead connect its properties to light-ring physics: correlations with remnant spin in numerical-relativity signals, an analytic merger-ringdown model built around the light ring, and similar residual signals from ultracompact objects without horizons. Filtering tests and a separate free-frequency fit help examine whether the observed component is a filtering artifact. The central distinction is between detecting a non-QNM contribution and establishing its physical origin. Within the systems studied, the evidence favors a light-ring association; it does not provide a universal decomposition of every nonlinear ringdown signal.
ai_review.relevance_reason: Directly addresses quasinormal modes, black-hole perturbation theory and ringdown interpretation, with useful connections between analytic models and numerical relativity.
ai_review.quality_reason: Several complementary tests confront the horizon-origin interpretation, including horizonless examples and alternative extraction methods. This offers substantial support within the studied models without making the physical decomposition unique.
ai_review.limitations: Selective reading of extracted HTML: abstract, filter checks and discussion/conclusion. Derivations, simulation data and figures were not independently verified. Extraction choices and the mapping between perturbative models and nonlinear merger signals remain relevant uncertainties.
ai_review.evidence_quote: morphologically similar non-QNM ringdown signals are produced by ultracompact objects with light rings but without event horizons

papers.title: SPLIT: Loosely-coherent inference of long-inspiral gravitational-wave sources for robustness against modeling and data outliers
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect gravitational waves (GWs) from dozens of extreme- and intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs/IMRIs). These sources will stay in-band for months to years, offering extraordinary scientific potential. However, their fully phase-coherent analysis standard in current pipelines imposes stringent waveform accuracy requirements; failing to model the signal over such long durations can result in significant systematic biases. To address this, we formulate a robust Bayesian inference framework that segments the data into blocks, infers each block coherently, and recombines the results using loosely-coherent phase information. By restricting full phase-tracking to much shorter block durations, this approach prevents significant accumulation of phase errors. We implement this methodology in \textsc{SPLIT} (Segmented Posteriors for Long-Inspiral Templates), a GPU-accelerated Python package. Applying \textsc{SPLIT} to an environment-rich injection, we demonstrate that while a fully-coherent vacuum-GR analysis incurs a maximum 1D systematic bias of $\approx 4.8σ$ from the truth, the shorter integration window of our loosely-coherent approach restricts such biases to $\lesssim 0.5σ$. Overall, despite a fractional loss of optimal signal-to-noise ratio, the substantial improvement in parameter accuracy offered by our method presents a highly advantageous trade-off for LISA and other future GW detectors.

papers.title: Vishveshwara's waveform revisited: insights from a Keldysh quasinormal mode expansion
papers.abstract: We revisit Vishveshwara's linear scattering on a Schwarzschild black hole to study the evolution of quasinormal mode activation along the full time-domain waveform. Specifically, by adopting a hyperboloidal approach we cast the scattering problem in a non-selfadjoint dynamics setting where a (Keldysh) resonant expansion in a bi-orthogonal system of quasinormal modes can be readily performed. The calculation reveals the neat correlation of the second peak in Vishveshwara's waveform to the fundamental mode and first overtones, closely following the ringdown waveform pattern of non-linear evolutions. The first peak is completely controlled, for even (Zerilli) perturbations, by the algebraically special mode and the nearby branch cut. This phenomenon is absent for odd (Regge-Wheeler) perturbations. These qualitative features are robust under change of initial data, extending to Reissner-Nordström and Kerr black holes but being absent when departing from asymptotic flatness to spacetime asymptotics without a branch cut. Underlying linear mechanisms might shed light on the role of algebraic speciality in the transition to the ringdown in non-linear evolutions.

papers.title: Cracking Gravitational Wave Multiple Ringdown Modes in Space
papers.abstract: Ringdown signals from perturbed black holes (BHs) offer a clean window into BH spacetime, strong-field gravity, and fundamental physics. Presently the quasi-normal modes of stellar-mass BH ringdowns have been successfully extracted in the ground-based gravitational wave (GW) observations. Looking ahead, the future space-borne observatories will listen to the ringdowns from massive BH binary coalescences more loudly and resolve multiple modes to unprecedented precision, which calls for efficient approaches to mitigate the sharply increasing computational burden. We develop a practical ringdown analysis pipeline for space-borne detectors by implementing FIREFLY, a novel acceleration algorithm validated in ground-based detectors, and for the first time demonstrate its compatibility and effectiveness with the time-delay interferometry (TDI) observables. With high fidelity, we achieve an over two-order-of-magnitude speedup for a simulated ringdown signal including six modes, providing a viable and scalable route for multi-mode ringdown analysis in the space context. This new approach has sound statistical interpretation and is extensible to other GW sources in band.

papers.title: Self-resonance preheating in deformed attractor models: oscillon formation and evolution
papers.abstract: It is well known that, in potentials that are quadratic near the minimum but shallower away, such as small-$α$ ($α\ll M_P^2$) attractors, the inflaton condensate fragments into localized compact objects known as oscillons during self-resonance preheating. In this work, we investigate self-resonance in a deformed $α$-attractor T-model with a Gaussian feature near the minimum, distant from the end of inflation. Linear analysis reveals altered resonance bands and deformed Floquet charts dependent on feature parameters, primarily through the localized modification of $V''(φ)$. In fully nonlinear lattice simulations, we find that the potential feature has only a modest influence on gradient-energy transfer during resonance, whereas the subsequent evolution becomes strongly dependent on the Gaussian feature's dimensionless amplitude $h$. Increasing $|h|$ suppresses the formation and persistence of compact oscillons, resulting in fewer objects and a smaller fraction of energy stored in them. The total-energy and internal-gradient-energy diagnostics give consistent lifetime trends. Within the directly resolved range, the oscillon lifetime decreases nonlinearly with increasing $|h|$, with negative $h$ generally producing shorter lifetimes than positive $h$ of the same magnitude. The gravitational wave emission is dominated by the resonant stage and becomes strongly suppressed after oscillon formation. We further find an enhancement in the high-frequency tail of the spectrum, sourced by the potential feature. Although a complete reheating description requires external couplings and higher-resolution simulations, clear qualitative differences in the post-inflationary expansion history already emerge within our simulated time window. These results clarify how potential features affect preheating dynamics and oscillon evolution.

papers.title: Modeling the merger-ringdown of an eccentric test-mass inspiral into a Kerr black hole using the effective-one-body framework
papers.abstract: We characterize and phenomenologically model the merger-ringdown of gravitational waves emitted by a small compact object that plunges and merges into a Kerr black hole from equatorial-eccentric inspirals. The waveforms are generated employing a time-domain Teukolsky code sourced with trajectories computed using the effective-one-body framework. We span values of the Kerr spin $a\in[-0.9, 0.9] $, eccentricity at the last stable orbit (LSO) $ e_{\rm LSO} \in [0,0.9] $, and relativistic anomaly $ ξ_{\rm LSO} \in [0 , 2 π]$. We characterize the last peak of the waveform and ringdown features across the parameter space, finding that the eccentricity mainly affects the last peak features, while it has a smaller impact on the ringdown signal. In contrast, the relativistic anomaly measured at the LSO influences the morphology of the last peak in a restricted portion of the parameter space and has no impact on the ringdown part. We perform the analysis for all the spin-weighted spherical harmonic modes normally included in the $\texttt{SEOBNR}$ family of models, $(\ell,m)\in\{ (2,2), (3,3), (4,4), (5,5), (2,1), (3,2), (4,3)\}$. Finally, we introduce a merger-ringdown model for $\texttt{SEOB-TMLE}$, a forthcoming inspiral-merger-ringdown waveform model for eccentric spin-aligned binary black holes in the test-mass limit, whose features can be extended to comparable-mass regimes. The model also accounts for quasinormal mode mixing during the ringdown. It provides a first step toward incorporating the impact of residual eccentricity close to merger into spin-aligned effective-one-body merger-ringdown models for binary black holes.

papers.title: Towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
papers.abstract: Near the threshold between scattering and capture by a Schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. Here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. The fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. Using the Wentzel, Kramers, and Brillouin (WKB) approximation to solve the Regge-Wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes. We then estimate the coefficients of the subleading pole contributions by combining numerical calculations at low multipoles with the exact asymptotics at large multipoles. We further conjecture an extension to equatorial circular orbits in Kerr. Interestingly, our results also inform the analytical structure of the energy and angular momentum losses of ultrarelativistic scattering orbits near the light ring. More broadly, our work illustrates how WKB methods can provide the asymptotic behavior of self-force observables in regimes where numerical mode sums become increasingly challenging.

papers.title: Cubic Quasinormal Modes in the Black-Hole Ringdown
papers.abstract: We formulate and numerically solve the nonlinear Teukolsky equations through third order, obtaining a first-principles calculation of cubic quasinormal-mode amplitudes for Kerr black holes. Our approach combines lower-order metric reconstruction in split light-cone gauges with a hyperboloidal, compactified formulation solved on complex radial contours. Spin-dependent complex coupling coefficients fix the cubic amplitudes from products of their linear parent amplitudes. We apply these predictions to a nonprecessing numerical-relativity waveform, including cubic products of the $(2,2)$ fundamental mode, its first overtone, and their conjugates. The predicted cubic terms improve agreement over selected early-ringdown fitting windows and shift inferred linear-overtone amplitudes without adding fitting parameters. $3M$ after the peak of $|h_{22}|$, the summed cubic contribution reaches approximately $38\%$ of the total $h_{22}$ signal; $M$ is the initial total mass. These results identify an appreciable cubic response in early ringdown.

papers.title: Hierarchical Parameter Estimation for Intrinsic Parameters of Extreme-mass-ratio Inspirals Using Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) stand as prime targets for future space-borne gravitational wave (GW) detectors, yet their precise parameter estimation is severely hindered by waveform complexity and high-dimensional parameter spaces. In this work, we propose a deep learning framework capable of recovering the seven intrinsic EMRI parameters without relying on detailed priors for extrinsic parameters. Our approach first employs a U-Net to extract robust signal features from noisy time-frequency data. These features are then fed into a multi-channel convolutional neural network (CNN) equipped with a dual attention mechanism, which decouples the time and frequency dimensions to jointly model long-range temporal evolution and persistent spectral structures, thereby enhancing sensitivity to EMRI time-frequency ridges in noisy data. Remarkably, this method reduces the search ranges for the parameters $\{\log M, a, μ, e_0, p_0 \}$ and $\{t_p, {x_I}_0 \}$ by factors of $\sim 10^{2}$ and $\sim 10^{1}$, respectively, effectively shrinking the total volume of the seven-dimensional parameter space by $\sim 10^{8}$. Such a dramatic reduction enables a rapid pre-screening of the intrinsic parameter space, substantially saving computational cost for subsequent full parameter estimation. Although our framework is developed with Taiji mission specifications in mind, the methodology is applicable to data from other space-borne GW detectors.

papers.title: Black Hole Fine Structure
papers.abstract: In General Relativity, axial and polar black-hole perturbations share identical quasinormal-mode spectra, a property known as isospectrality. New physics can break this degeneracy, producing a spectral splitting analogous to atomic fine structure. We perform a theory-agnostic search for such splitting in gravitational-wave observations. We find no evidence for isospectrality breaking and place a combined $90\%$ upper limit of $<28.5\%$ on the relative frequency splitting. We map these constraints onto several modified-gravity theories, constraining the coupling-lengths to be $\lesssim 28\,\mathrm{km}$.

papers.title: Strong Field Gravitational Lensing in Full Wave Optics
papers.abstract: Compact binaries evolving in the vicinity of massive black holes may be commonplace in the Universe, and their gravitational waves carry signatures of their environment. We study the strong lensing of these signals by the massive companion, a configuration that violates the standard assumptions of the lensing literature: geometric optics and thin lenses. Using a perturbative framework, we compute the full wave optics amplification factors for face-on and edge-on binaries, including spinning lenses. In the edge-on configuration, peak amplification does not occur at perfect source--lens--observer alignment, even for a non-spinning lens. This is a consequence of the anisotropic, coherent quadrupolar emission of the stellar-mass binary breaking the axisymmetry of the system. Restricting to the equatorial plane near the optical axis, we then find that the frequency dependence of the amplification factor is universal across every configuration studied, persisting deep into the wave optics regime. Comparing against a strong-field ray tracing calculation, we find agreement at the $\sim10\%$ level for a face-on binary lensed by a Schwarzschild black hole. In the less symmetric edge-on case only the angular peak shift and fringe spacing is reproduced to this accuracy. For a Kerr lens, the face-on amplification factor is described by its Schwarzschild counterpart to the same $\sim 10 \%$ accuracy once the effect of frame dragging is corrected for. A point mass lens, by contrast, fails to reproduce the features of the system, which may have strong implications for forecasts that adopt it for lensing by massive black holes in the strong field.

papers.title: EMRIs in Kerr Spacetime: The Role of Inclination Diffusion
papers.abstract: Extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are expected to be a major source of gravitational waves (GWs) for the future {\it Laser Interferometer Space Antenna} ({\it LISA}). An EMRI occurs when a compact object, driven by the emission of gravitational radiation, slowly inspirals into a massive black hole (MBH). The classical formation channel involves repeated two-body interactions within dense nuclear star clusters. However, both EMRI event rates and the expected distribution of their orbital parameters remain highly uncertain. A major source of this uncertainty is the poorly constrained ratio between gradually inspiraling EMRIs and direct plunges, which do not produce detectable GWs. While most studies of astrophysical EMRI production focus on the Schwarzschild limit, previous work examining the Kerr metric found that the spin of the central MBH can significantly affect the EMRI-to-plunge ratio. This enhancement depends sensitively on orbital inclination, yet earlier studies held inclination fixed. In this work, we develop the mathematical framework describing inclination evolution driven by two-body encounters evolving along Kerr geodesics. By implementing 3D diffusion into Monte Carlo simulations, we show that initially prograde orbits may evolve into retrograde states, thereby converting potential EMRIs into plunges or vice versa. We estimate the EMRI-to-plunge ratio and find that substantial MBH spin enhances the EMRI rate by a factor of $\sim 2.5$. Additionally, even for a non-spinning MBH, modeling the orbits as relativistic geodesics rather than Newtonian trajectories increases the number of EMRIs by a similar factor of $\sim 2.5$. The distribution of Kerr EMRI inclinations has a substantial prograde bias that may aid in identifying the subset of loss cone EMRIs within large future EMRI samples.

papers.title: Turning Selection Bias into a New Statistic: Asymmetry and Fringes of Lensed Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagating across the Universe can be distorted by intervening lenses, producing characteristic wave-optics signatures. These effects are not incorporated into current matched-filtering searches and can therefore substantially reduce detection efficiency. The underlying mechanism is the signal-consistency test, which measures deviations between the observed and expected signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions. We report a systematic study of the impact of gravitational lensing on signal-consistency tests, using a two-image interference model and representative signal-consistency statistics in both the time and frequency domains. We find that overlapping images produce sharply localized SNR residuals in the time domain, breaking the reflection symmetry of the autocorrelation about the merger time. Although interference fringes produce broadband SNR residuals in the frequency domain, both domains exhibit a minimum for high-mass signals when the fringe structure becomes comparable to the signal bandwidth. This highlights a limitation of current strategies that search for distorted lensed signals only among GW events detected by matched-filtering searches. Exploiting this asymmetry, we develop a statistic that separates selected down-ranked lensed injections from noise-background triggers and paired nonlensed injections, without extending the template bank. Our results establish the first connection between lensing observables and detection, paving the way for the discovery of lensed GWs.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated Bayesian inference for diffracted gravitational wave signals
papers.abstract: As the rate of gravitational wave detections continues to grow, the probability of observing a gravitationally lensed gravitational wave also increases. When the Schwarzschild radius of the lens is comparable in size to the gravitational wave wavelength, wave-optics effects induce a frequency- dependent modulation on the signal. CPU-based parameter estimation analyses for wave-optics lensing are computationally intensive, limiting the scale of studies to determine the significance of any potential lensing candidate. In this work, we implement a point-mass lens model in Jim, a high-performance GPU-based parameter estimation pipeline. This enables, for the first time, GPU-accelerated Bayesian inference in full-wave optics, including the computation of Bayes factors, without the need for training data. We call this framework Jim-lensing. Using this framework, we are able to speed up a full parameter estimation run under the point-mass lens hypothesis from more than 10 hours to the order of 10 minutes compared to the current state-of-the-art CPU-based pipeline. We show that our implementation is stable and obtains comparable results to this state-of- the-art pipeline. The substantial speed gain over existing CPU pipelines paves the way for analyzing gravitational wave data under a broader range of lensing models with greater capacity to produce robust frequentist significance estimates.

papers.title: Outer trapped surface formation from gravitational waves collision
papers.abstract: We give a new rigorous construction of outer trapped surface formation in smooth vacuum spacetimes without symmetry assumptions. The outer trapped surface is produced by the collision of two transversely localized, nearly plane-fronted gravitational waves described by short pulse data. The outer trapped surface is obtained by joining two smooth pieces along a curve with their future-directed outer null normals matching continuously. The incompleteness of the maximal future development is then established by adapting Penrose's original argument. This construction is inspired by Penrose's argument in constructing a marginally outer trapped surface in the collision of two ultra-relativistic particles modeled by the Aichelburg--Sexl solution.

papers.title: Nanohertz gravitational waves from domain walls nucleated during inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) produced by domain walls (DWs) nucleated via quantum tunneling during inflation with an extended nucleation time. In contrast to the small-period nucleation framework, in which DWs form over a narrow interval and possess nearly identical radii, we show that an extended nucleation period leads to a distribution of DW radii characterized by $γ\equiv\overline{R^{10}}/(\overline{R^5})^2>1$, which enhances the resulting curvature perturbations. We construct a two-field inflation model with an inflaton $φ$ and a spectator field $χ$ coupled through the potential $V(φ,χ)$, where the DW tension $σ(t)$ evolves smoothly as the inflaton rolls past a critical value. The characteristic width of this transition determines the cutoff scale $k_{\text{cut}}$ of the curvature power spectrum, enabling the SIGW peak to be placed in the nanohertz frequency band with detectable amplitude. For three representative parameter sets, we compute the SIGW spectra and find that the peak frequency ranges from $\sim10^{-8}$\,Hz to $\sim10^{-1}$\,Hz, with the nanohertz-peaked spectrum matching the NANOGrav and EPTA signals for suitable parameter choices. By selecting different parameters, our model can produce signals detectable by different gravitational-wave detectors.

papers.title: MADGRAV: a multilevel anomaly-detection pipeline for gravitational-wave searches applied to LIGO data
papers.abstract: We present the results of \textbf{MADGRAV}, a deep-learning-based search for high-mass compact binary coalescences, applied to the data collected by the LIGO interferometers during the third observing run and during the first and second part of the fourth observing run. The \textbf{MADGRAV} pipeline consists of a series of sequential convolutional neural networks that perform anomaly detection, glitch classification, coherence testing, and signal ranking. Data from the Hanford and Livingston LIGO detectors are studied (both individually and in coherence) by way of 1 second Q-transform windows. Of the candidates that survive every stage of the pipeline, 48 reach the significance threshold, and we report 47 gravitational wave detections characterised by a false alarm rate below $1\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_{\rm astro}>0.9$. Of the 47 detections, 44 are shared with the minimally modelled coherent WaveBurst search. The observed total source-frame masses, extracted from official gravitational wave transient catalogues, are in the $14-236 M_{\odot}$ range with a median of $69 M_{\odot}$, and a median SNR of 16. We note that the recovered fraction of confident detections rises with mass: for LIGO detectors network SNR $>10$ the pipeline recovers $8.1\%$ of confident catalog events below $30 M_{\odot}$, $39.8\%$ between $30$ and $100 M_{\odot}$, and $53.3\%$ above $100 M_{\odot}$, corresponding to $33.3\%$, $45.5\%$ and $53.3\%$ of the events detected by coherent WaveBurst in the same bins. These results suggest that anomaly detection pipelines can serve as an independent detection channel complementary to matched filtering in the high-mass high-SNR regime.

papers.title: Constraints on the Cosmic Expansion Rate Using the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey and the Fifth Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave standard sirens provide a calibration-free measure of distances, offering important input on the long-standing tension between early- and late-Universe measurements of the Hubble constant ($H_0$). In the absence of an electromagnetic counterpart, the dark siren method can be employed to statistically correlate a gravitational wave event's localization with a galaxy catalog of potential hosts. We present a measurement of the Hubble constant using the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey Data Release 3 and the fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog. Applying the dark siren method to a large, photometrically heterogeneous footprint required revised catalog-construction choices: a faint apparent-magnitude threshold ($m_r<20$) to control known photometric-redshift bias, a bright apparent-magnitude threshold ($m_r>15.5$) to exclude saturated sources, implementation of an evolving luminosity function parameterization, and de-biasing survey regions based on survey depth and photometric redshift precision. With these choices applied to DELVE, we obtain $H_0= 67.4^{+13.0}_{-11.2}\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ from dark sirens alone, and $H_0= 70.6^{+8.7}_{-7.0}\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ when combined with the bright siren GW170817. We test other galaxy catalog configuration choices, and find subdominant influence from photometric band choice and luminosity function parameterization on the final $H_0$ posterior. Our results demonstrate that extending the dark siren method to wider-area, non-uniform galaxy surveys is feasible and provides additional constraining power on $H_0$ relative to the spectral siren method, opening the door for analyses with forthcoming galaxy catalogs from LSST, Euclid, and Roman.

papers.title: Probing Compact Binary Coalescences in the Decihertz GW Band with IndIGO-D
papers.abstract: We present an astrophysical science-case study of IndIGO-D, a decihertz gravitational-wave mission concept, focusing on compact binary sources across the 0.1-10 Hz band bridging LISA and next-generation ground-based interferometers. For these science projections, we consider three spacecraft forming an L-shaped interferometer in a heliocentric orbit, with two orthogonal 1000 km arms sharing a common vertex. We calculate the time-dependent antenna response of this geometry, including modulation produced by the orbital motion of the constellation. We treat the strain-sensitivity curve supplied by the IndIGO-D collaboration as an input. For the assumed sensitivity, we estimate a BNS detection rate of $\sim76$-$767\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. We compute horizon distances for different source classes and find that intermediate-mass black-hole binaries with masses $10^2$-$10^3\,M_\odot$ are detectable throughout their formation history, complementing the reach of LISA and terrestrial detectors. Binary neutron star systems are observable to a horizon redshift of $z\lesssim0.3$, allowing continuous multi-band coverage with Voyager-class interferometers from the decihertz regime to merger. A Bayesian parameter-estimation study of a GW170817-like binary shows that the sky localization area improves from $\sim21\,{\rm deg}^2$ at one month, $\sim1\,{\rm deg}^2$ at one week, down to $0.3\,{\rm deg}^2$ at six hours pre-merger. These sky areas are readily tiled by the Rubin Observatory, whose $9.6\,{\rm deg}^2$ field of view and r-band depth enable high-cadence, repeated coverage of GW170817-like kilonovae at this distance and beyond. IndIGO-D bridges the gap between millihertz and terrestrial observations, enabling early warnings on timescales from months to hours and enhancing the prospects for multi-band and multi-messenger discoveries. (abridged)

papers.title: Hostbusters: constraining $H_0$ and binary formation channels through gravitational-wave host galaxy associations
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave dark sirens can be combined with galaxy catalogues to provide a measurement of the Hubble constant. This inference requires assigning each potential host galaxy a probability of hosting a merger, but the appropriate weighting is uncertain because the binary merger rate may trace different galaxy properties, such as stellar mass or star formation rate, depending on the underlying formation channel. We introduce a flexible framework in which the dark-siren population is described as a mixture of two host-weighting prescriptions, with the mixing fraction inferred jointly with $H_0$. These components may be interpreted as subpopulations associated with distinct binary-formation environments. Using simulated catalogues, we show that marginalising over uncertainty in the host-population mixture preserves unbiased constraints on $H_0$, while allowing the gravitational-wave data to constrain the relative contribution of the two host populations. In particular, an A#-like detector network with $\mathcal{O}(10^3)$ dark sirens may be able to exclude scenarios in which the host population traces only one of the two weighting prescriptions. Dark-siren analyses may therefore provide robust cosmological measurements and new information about how merging compact binaries trace the galaxy population.

papers.title: Searching for Extra Dimensions with Gravitational Waves: Dark-Siren Constraints from GWTC-4
papers.abstract: Higher-dimensional theories of gravity predict that gravitational waves (GWs) can propagate into extra spatial dimensions, leading to modified amplitude damping over cosmological distances. Measurements of GW luminosity distances therefore provide a unique probe of the dimensionality of spacetime. In this work, we constrain higher-dimensional GW propagation using the dark-siren method with the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog 4.0 (GWTC-4). We adopt a phenomenological parameterization motivated by braneworld scenarios, in which deviations from General Relativity are characterized by the spacetime dimension number $D$ and a crossover scale $R_c$ governing the transition between four- and higher-dimensional gravity. We perform a hierarchical Bayesian analysis combining 141 compact binary coalescences from GWTC-4 with line-of-sight galaxy information from the GLADE+ catalog. For a prior $H_0 \in [65,77]\ {\rm km~s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\log(R_c/{\rm Mpc}) \in [2.7,4.0]$, we obtain $D = 4.38^{+1.91}_{-1.01}$ (68\% credible interval). We also find that the inferred posterior distribution of $R_c$ accumulates near the upper prior boundary, indicating that the crossover scale remains poorly constrained by current observations. We further show that the inferred constraint on $D$ depends sensitively on the assumed prior range of $R_c$, which determines the characteristic distance scale at which deviations from General Relativity become significant. Our results provide the first GWTC-4 dark-siren constraints on higher-dimensional GW propagation and demonstrate that current observations remain consistent with four-dimensional General Relativity.

papers.title: Gravitational Wave Propagation in K-essence Cosmology: Theory and Observational Constraints
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a powerful, theory-independent probe of the dynamical structure of spacetime and the cosmological background. We investigate the propagation of linearized tensor modes in k-essence cosmology, where the dark sector is described by a non-canonical scalar field. Working in the high-frequency (short-wavelength) limit on a Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker background and restricting to the transverse-traceless sector, we obtain a modified evolution equation in which the GW speed remains strictly luminal (compatible with GW170817), while the background field $\barφ$ generates a time-dependent effective mass term $m_{\rm eff}$. This background-induced mass alters the dispersion relation without introducing extra propagating degrees of freedom, producing an accumulated, frequency-dependent phase shift over cosmological distances. We show that $m_{\rm eff}$ is uniquely determined by background cosmological parameters and can be expressed as a redshift-dependent function $m_{\rm eff}(z)$, providing a direct connection between GW observables and scalar-field dynamics. The GW luminosity distance stays identical to the electromagnetic one, preserving standard-siren consistency. We confront the model with a joint Bayesian analysis combining cosmic chronometers, BAO, Pantheon+SH0ES, and standard-siren measurements from GWTC-2.1/3/4, and assess performance using $χ^2$, $χ^2_{\rm red}$, AIC, BIC, and DIC. The reconstruction is consistent with current data, reproduces the late-time expansion history, and provides data-driven constraints on the redshift evolution of $m_{\rm eff}(z)$.

papers.title: Axial Mode Stability and Quasinormal Modes of Charged Kiselev Black Holes in Rastall Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate axial gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of charged black holes surrounded by dust-like Kiselev-type anisotropic matter in Rastall gravity. We derive the axial matter compatibility condition and construct a compatible response by holding the covariant anisotropy-direction vector unperturbed. The resulting gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations obey two coupled Schrodinger-type master equations. An r-independent algebraic decoupling exists in the Reissner-Nordstrom and general-relativistic dust-like limits; additional radial structure obstructs it in generic charged Rastall backgrounds with nonzero surrounding matter. We prove axial mode stability under the adopted closure for every nonextremal background satisfying the stated exterior conditions, covering all physical axial multipoles. A matrix S-deformation excludes exponentially growing coupled modes for l >= 2, while the physical electromagnetic dipole has a positive effective potential. A Chebyshev pseudospectral calculation, validated against the Reissner-Nordstrom spectrum and spectral convergence, determines the fundamental frequencies. In the parameter ranges examined, increasing the Rastall coupling lowers both the oscillation frequency and the damping rate in the small-coupling region; in the large-coupling region, the oscillation frequency rises while the damping rate varies nonmonotonically. A larger charge generally raises the oscillation frequency, whereas stronger surrounding-matter contributions produce longer-lived modes.

papers.title: Gravitational lensing effects on neutrino oscillations around a Schwarzschild black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
papers.abstract: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the weak gravitational-lensing regime of a static, spherically symmetric black hole surrounded by perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM). Within a covariant quantum-mechanical framework, we derive the oscillation phases for radial and non-radial propagation of ultrarelativistic neutrinos. While the leading radial phase is independent of the metric function, non-radial trajectories acquire impact-parameter-dependent corrections governed by the PFDM parameter $λ$. We construct the flavor-transition probability for two coherent lensed paths and analyze the resulting interference in two and three flavor scenarios. Varying $λ$ shifts the oscillation extrema and modifies their amplitudes and contrast, with a non-monotonic dependence on the neutrino mass scale, lens mass, flavor channel, and mass ordering. The $P_{μτ}$ channel shows particularly strong sensitivity to the PFDM contribution for the considered configurations. Moreover, the path-interference terms retain information about the absolute neutrino mass scale. These results characterize PFDM-induced modifications of lensed neutrino oscillations and provide a basis for more realistic treatments including decoherence, averaging, detector resolution, and corrections to lens trajectories and magnifications.

papers.title: Tidal Heating of Stellar Clusters in Fuzzy Dark Matter Halos
papers.abstract: Ultra-faint dwarf galaxies serve as powerful testing grounds for wave dark matter models through dynamical stellar heating. Previous simulation-based work derived a lower bound on the fuzzy dark matter particle mass using a diffusion approximation valid only when the de Broglie wavelength is much smaller than the galaxy's half-light radius. We simulate the dynamical evolution of stellar clusters in FDM halos across a wide mass range and find that for sufficiently low masses, where the de Broglie wavelength is much larger than the cluster size, tidal heating is the main mechanism. We also find that a reduced soliton mass and tidally stripped halo can suppress the heating. We demonstrate that in order to constrain FDM mass from cluster heating, the structure and environment of the FDM halo must be carefully considered.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes as probes of black hole reentrant phase transitions
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between thermodynamic phase transitions and the dynamical behavior of quasi-normal modes (QNMs) in weakly nonlinear charged anti-de Sitter black holes. In a non-extended phase space, we identify a reentrant large-small-large(intermediate) phase transition for these black holes. Employing the shooting method to solve the Klein-Gordon equation for a massless scalar field, we compute QNM frequencies across these phases, revealing distinct behaviors in different phases. Specifically, to our knowledge, this is the first report of utilizing QNMs as dynamical probes of thermodynamic phases during reentrant phase transitions including zeroth and first-order transitions. These findings establish QNMs as a powerful dynamical probe for thermodynamic phase transitions, providing new insights into the thermodynamic and dynamical properties of nonlinear charged black holes as well.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from cosmic superstrings and gauge strings
papers.abstract: We perform a phenomenological comparison of the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum expected from cosmic gauge string networks and superstring networks comprised of multiple string types. We show how violations of scaling behavior and the evolution of the number of relativistic degrees of freedom in the early Universe affect the GW spectrum. We derive simple analytical expressions for the GW spectrum from superstrings and gauge strings that are valid for all frequencies relevant to pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and laser interferometers. We analyze the latest data from PTAs and show that superstring networks are consistent with 32 nHz data from NANOGrav, but are excluded by 3.2 nHz data at $3σ$ unless the string coupling $g_s<0.2$ or the strings evolve in only about 10% of the volume of the higher-dimensional space. We also point out that while gauge string networks are excluded by NANOGrav-15 data at $3σ$, they are completely compatible with EPTA and PPTA data. Finally, we study correlations between GW signals at PTAs and laser interferometers.

papers.title: The efficiency gap of two-step forecasts for stochastic gravitational wave background searches
papers.abstract: The stochastic gravitational-wave background is targeted by the millihertz observatories LISA, Taiji and TianQin, and its forecast precision rests on a Whittle approximation to the periodogram likelihood. The quoted scale is that of a joint fit a two-step forecast need not reach. We show that the residual risk of a two-step forecast lies in the estimator route rather than in the likelihood. At the exact Whittle form we separate the forecast error into a deterministic bias $\mathbf{b}$ and an efficiency gap $\mathbf{C}_b$, both in closed form. We find that this gap is governed by the span of the first-step nuisance fit. It decreases substantially as the span increases and vanishes when the first-step fit spans the entire band or when the response exhibits no within-bin structure. The gap does not arise as a cost of the prior. Across the LISA band the gap spans more than an order of magnitude, the amplitude and tilt inflation falling from about thirty and twenty to unity at a band-wide first step. A foreground from the released LDC2a population moves the mid-band gap by an order of magnitude. A two-step forecast should therefore report the span of its first-step fit with its intervals, since that span decides whether they sit at the Fisher scale or an order of magnitude above it.

papers.title: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation with machine-learning generated surrogate waveforms
papers.abstract: The worldwide network of gravitational-wave detectors have detected more than 350 binary coalescence events till date. Future third-generation detectors, like Einstein telescope, are expected to detect orders-of-magnitude more signals from sources with more complicated characteristics, including eccentric orbits and high-mass ratio binaries. It is well-established that the computational cost of parameter estimation for signals from these kinds of sources will be extremely high. In particular, the process could be sped-up if generating theoretical waveform predictions, used for likelihood calculation becomes faster. Recently, various machine-learning techniques has been proposed to this end. In this work, we propose a two-stage deterministic conditional-autoencoder model for generating four-parameter SEOBNRv4 waveforms. The first-stage of the model generates amplitude and phase series of the waveform, while the second-stage calibrates the residual error in the predictions. Our model achieves a median mismatch of around $10^{-2}$ with the target polarization waveforms, while the calibrated amplitude/phase series achieve $10^{-6}$ level cosine distance error. We then propose a waveform conditioning step to enable use of these surrogate waveforms for downstream parameter estimation tasks. Finally, we perform extensive parameter estimation tests, with ML and EOB waveform injections and try to recover posterior estimates for the source parameters. We find that when ML waveforms are used to recover EOB target parameter estimates, the inferred posterior have some systematic bias. This inherent bias can be estimated and corrected for, and then importance reweighting of posterior samples can enable use of low-accuracy surrogate waveforms at low SNRs.

papers.title: Multimessenger Probes of Primordial Black Holes with Gravitational Wave and 21 cm Observations
papers.abstract: Primordial black holes (PBHs) formed from the collapse of curvature perturbations in the early universe are known to have an associated gravitational wave signal sourced by the same scalar perturbations. In this work, we show that there is a complementarity between these gravitational waves and modifications of the 21 cm global signal during the cosmic dark ages due to PBH evaporation. For PBHs in the range $ M_{\rm PBH} \sim 5 \times 10^{13} \, {\rm g} - 10^{17} \, {\rm g}$, there is a correlated signal in gravitational waves in the LISA, deci-Hz, and ground based regimes from $f_{\rm GW} \sim 10^{-3} \, {\rm Hz} - 20 \, {\rm Hz}$ and in the 21 cm global signal from $z \sim 300 - 30$. These observations are entirely independent of each other and within the reach of near-future experiments, making a combined measurement a novel multimessenger probe of primordial physics.

papers.title: Gravitational Waves as a Probe of Multi-Fluid Cosmologies: General Formalism and the Case of Cosmological Stasis
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) provide a powerful probe of the expansion history of the universe prior to the Big Bang. Indeed, the production of such gravity waves depends on the evolution of first-order scalar perturbations within the early universe, while their subsequent propagation depends on the background equation of state. In this paper we extend previous discussions by studying SIGWs in cosmologies containing multiple fluids. As we shall demonstrate, the gravitational-wave signal within such multi-fluid cosmologies is modified in two distinct ways: not only are there new velocity effects which have no single-fluid analogues, but there are also significant alterations to the subsequent redshifting of modes that enter the horizon before the multi-fluid era ends. Thus SIGWs provide a probe of not only the overall expansion rate within such cosmologies, but also their internal multi-fluid composition. As an example, we then consider the case of gravitational waves arising during an epoch of cosmological stasis. During such an epoch, the abundances of energy components with different equations of state remain constant, thereby giving rise to a universe with a constant effective equation of state which nevertheless remains genuinely multi-fluid despite cosmological expansion. Despite their constant equations of state, we find that such stasis cosmologies also give rise to tensor power spectra and present-day gravitational-wave abundances which are significantly different from those expected within a standard radiation-dominated universe.

papers.title: Exceptional points and near-extremal boundary response in rotating BTZ black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate whether the coalescence of long-lived quasinormal modes enhances the boundary response of rotating BTZ black holes. Using exact scalar solutions with mixed Robin boundary conditions and the retarded boundary correlator, we compare frequency-domain resonances and time-domain signals at fixed source and operator normalizations. An exceptional point (EP) can be crossed by varying the spin alone in a suitably selected fixed theory. Along a distinct near-extremal path that tracks the co-rotating EP surface by tuning the scalar mass and boundary coupling, a taller, narrower resonance coexists with a weaker but longer-lasting double-pole impulse response. The frequency-domain enhancement persists away from the EP and is therefore not unique to mode coalescence. Thus, the EP determines the double-pole structure and Jordan relaxation, but does not by itself determine the response strength, which also depends on the physical path and excitation protocol.

papers.title: Prospects for Simultaneously Detecting Long and Short Duration Gravitational Waves from Pulsar Glitches with Current and Future Detectors
papers.abstract: The internal mechanisms that drive the sudden change in rotation frequency in pulsar glitches could emit gravitational waves (GWs) at multiple time scales. The potential for GW analyses to detect both long and short forms of emission ("tCW-like" and "burst-like") improves as the detectors increase in sensitivity. We aim to examine how future detectors fare in making this joint measurement. By examining past glitches from the ATNF catalog, we quantify the double-detectability prospects of current- and next-generation GW detector networks. We further explore what astrophysical constraints could be placed following a double non-detection using extrapolations from the 2024 Vela pulsar glitch as a stand-in example. We find that a network with at least one next-generation detector greatly increases the probability of double-detection for many known glitching pulsars and improves the detection threshold in glitch energy by nearly two orders of magnitude over existing LIGO detectors.
