Additionally, double non-detections with networks with at least one next-generation detector could place dramatically improved limits on properties of the pulsar.

papers.title: From the Test-Mass Limit to Binary Black-Hole Waveforms in Higher-Derivative Gravity
papers.abstract: Many higher-derivative theories predict stronger deviations from General Relativity for lower-mass black holes, while their nonlinear field equations often prevent reliable simulations of the full binary evolution. Here we develop a route from controlled black hole perturbation theory based on the modified Teukolsky formalism to comparable-mass waveforms, using parity-even cubic gravity as a representative example. We find that the tidal response of the secondary black hole enters at the same perturbative order as the direct higher-curvature correction and is therefore essential for a consistent leading-order waveform. The resulting strong-field fluxes and conservative dynamics produce an accumulated inspiral dephasing that grows toward merger. Embedding this test-mass information into an effective-one-body model, we construct inspiral-merger-ringdown waveforms for comparable-mass binaries and find coupling-dependent dephasing and waveform-peak shifts. Our results demonstrate how strong-field test-mass calculations can anchor waveform models for higher-derivative gravity when theory-specific numerical-relativity simulations are unavailable.

papers.title: Strong Lensing and Quasinormal modes of a Black Hole with a Global Monopole
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate various key aspects of a static and spherically symmetric black hole with a global monopole. Firstly, we analyze the deflection angle in the strong field limit of a spacetime with a global monopole. It shows that the angle of deflection increases when the two characteristic parameters for the monopole configuration, $η$ and $λ$, increase. The influence of the global monopole parameter on the lensing observables and the black hole shadow is studied. This shows that a larger monopole parameter corresponds to larger shadow radii. The dynamics of timelike geodesics is also investigated in the spacetime. General circular orbits and the innermost stable circular orbits (ISCO) of timelike particles are discussed, highlighting that the monopole parameter significantly affects the circular orbits and the ISCO. In particular, it is observed that the radius of ISCO rises monotonically with $η$. In addition, the Lyapunov exponent is used to analyze the stability of timelike geodesics. We also determine the quasinormal modes under electromagnetic perturbations for different values of $η$. Our findings indicate that increasing the monopole parameter gives rise to electromagnetic perturbations with more slowly damped oscillations. To further validate the derived quasinormal mode spectrum, we discuss the time-domain evolution of the perturbation, confirming the presence of the characteristic quasinormal ringing followed by late-time power-law tails. Finally, comparison with the EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A* determines the parameter combinations of $η$ and $λ$ compatible with current observations, and the observational prospects of the strong-lensing observables are discussed.

papers.title: Quadrupole and quadratic-in-spin effects in quasicircular, spinning, asymmetric binaries
papers.abstract: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors will require significant improvements in current theoretical waveform models, particularly in the case of asymmetric-mass binaries. Here we provide one such improvement by calculating fully relativistic finite-size effects for small mass ratios -- primarily, fluxes of energy -- including quadratic-in-secondary-spin terms, spin-induced quadrupole terms, and tidally induced quadrupole terms, for quasicircular inspirals of a small companion into a Kerr black hole. We formulate these calculations within a multiscale waveform-generation framework in self-force theory, which could be used, with an energy-balance law we derive, to develop self-contained waveform models for asymmetric binaries involving stars orbiting black holes. Our results could additionally be used to improve other families of waveform models across all mass ratios. We present results both as complete numerical data sets on a Chebyshev grid and as analytical post-Newtonian expansions (to sixth PN order relative to the leading term in each contribution to the flux).

papers.title: Axial gravitational quasinormal modes of magnetically charged black holes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider axial perturbations on the magnetically charged string-inspired Euler-Heisenberg black hole. Since axial metric perturbation decouples from axial electromagnetic perturbation, here we mainly focus on axial gravitational perturbation. By using WKB approximation and AIM methods, we make a detailed analysis of the gravitational quasinormal frequencies by varying the characteristic parameters of gravitational perturbation and black holes. It is found these results obtained through the AIM method are in good agreement with those of obtained by WKB method, including these results extracted from the time-domain profiles. The greybody factor is calculated by WKB method. The effects of these parameters $Q_m$, $ε$ and multipole number $l$ on the greybody factor are also studied.

papers.title: Mock Catalogs of Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves via a Halo Model Approach with Space-borne Detectors
papers.abstract: Future space-borne gravitational-wave (GW) detectors, such as LISA and DECIGO, are expected to detect a large number of GW events, a fraction of which may be strongly lensed by intervening galaxies or galaxy clusters. In this work, we develop a comprehensive framework to simulate strongly lensed GWs in the context of space-borne detectors. Based on realistic astrophysical models for both the source population and the lens distribution, we construct mock catalogs of lensed GW events, referred to as \textbf{GW-LMC-Space}. Our results show that, for a four-year LISA observation, the expected number of lensed events ranges from $0$ to $131$, depending on the adopted formation model of massive black hole binaries (MBHBs). The corresponding lensing probability for MBHBs can reach up to $\sim 0.3\%$. For DECIGO, we find that the number of lensed events in a one-year observation is expected to lie in the range of $0$--$44$, with a lensing probability of $\sim 0.15\%$ for stellar-mass binary black holes (BBHs), binary neutron stars (BNSs), and neutron star--black hole binaries (NSBHs). We further show that the overlap of lensed signals is a common feature in space-borne detectors, which can significantly affect both the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimation and event identification. These results highlight the importance of accounting for signal overlap in the analysis of strongly lensed GW events in future space-borne GW observations.

papers.title: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $α_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $γ=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $λ_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|α_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}α_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANLγ/λ_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.

papers.title: FUGUE: A New GPU-accelerated General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics Code with Weak-Field Multipole Self-Gravity and Quasi-Stationary Kerr Black Hole Evolution
papers.abstract: We present FUGUE, a new GPU-accelerated code for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD). The code supports an optional quasi-stationary update of the Kerr black hole mass and spin, as well as weak-field multipole self-gravity computed with a spherical harmonic Poisson solver. The calculations using high-order multipoles in the Poisson solver are expensive, so the self-gravity solver is well suited for GPU acceleration. The code uses shock-capturing methods and a second-order Runge--Kutta (RK2) scheme for time integration. We validate the code with hydrodynamic, magnetohydrodynamic, general relativistic, and convergence tests for the self-gravity module. We present an application of the code to a simulation of a self-gravitating, Toomre-unstable, magnetized accretion disk with a mass of 1,M-Sun around a Kerr black hole. In our demonstration model, gravitational instabilities are associated with changes in the mass accretion rate and the Blandford--Znajek luminosity, and may contribute to gamma-ray burst variability.The performance of the code is equivalent to or exceeds that of the current state-of-the-art GRMHD codes, achieving more than 470 million zone-cycles per second on a single NVIDIA GH200 GPU with linear reconstruction.

papers.title: Co-design of ground-based gravitational wave detector networks
papers.abstract: Discussions around the design philosophy and location of the next generation of ground-based gravitational wave detectors are still underway. In this context, we propose IfoScout, an innovative methodology for detector co-design based on state-of-the-art machine-learning (ML) techniques. As a simple demonstration, we present a two-stage simulation of a network of fictional L-shaped interferometers whose sensitivity is optimized within physical and geographical constraints, indirectly resulting in reducing the costs. To achieve this, we gather publicly available data for two token locations and establish the length and orientation with reinforcement learning (RL). Next, we optimize the internal detector parameters related to cavity stability to achieve the best possible sensitivity by means of differential programming (DP). We make the case that pipelines such as IfoScout could have a positive impact on the final design of new generation detectors (e.g. the Einstein Telescope, the Cosmic Explorer, etc.), given precise data and detailed, realistic simulations of the interferometers.

papers.title: Optimal Strategies for Gravitational-Wave Memory Detection with Noise Marginalization in Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.abstract: Current pulsar timing arrays could detect gravitational wave memory, which would provide a unique test of general relativity. In order to optimize our searches for gravitational wave memory in pulsar timing arrays, we integrate the optimal frequentist statistics for GW memory into the \texttt{enterprise} code suite. We additionally test a noise marginalized version of this statistic, and compare it's effectiveness to the simpler maximum posterior method. We perform these tests on simulated pulsar timing array with red and white noise content, as well as the NANOGrav $15$-year data set. We find no significant variations in our detection statistics between the noise-marginalized and the maximum-posterior methods for the simulated datasets, and only small variations in the NANOGrav $15$-year comparisons. We conclude that for realistic PTAs the noise-marginalization method could be useful for assigning a false alarm probability to Bayesian results, though the maximum posterior method is sufficient for identifying potentially detectable signals.

papers.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
papers.abstract: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

papers.title: Leptogenesis with a GeV-Scale Quasi-Dirac Neutrino
papers.abstract: We discuss leptogenesis in a model with a GeV-scale quasi-Dirac neutral lepton, comprising mainly sterile states, which is accessible to future experiments. In particular, we show that Higgs-decay leptogenesis can naturally arise from the type-I seesaw mechanism with spontaneously broken global lepton number together with a discrete $Z_2$ symmetry, yielding two quasi-degenerate right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) which, to excellent approximation, form a single Dirac neutrino, with a tiny mass splitting as required for resonant enhancement generated by higher-dimensional lepton-number-violating operators. Incorporating finite-temperature effects, we show that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully generated through thermal Higgs decays for 0.1-10 GeV mass quasi-Dirac neutrinos, with the CP asymmetry arising from the interplay between the vacuum and thermal contributions to the mass splitting. In the parameter region of successful leptogenesis, the quasi-Dirac neutrino is accessible to future heavy neutral lepton searches at SHiP, MATHUSLA and FCC-ee. In addition, the same symmetry-breaking sector gives rise to unstable domain walls whose annihilation can generate a stochastic gravitational-wave background, providing a complementary probe of the framework.

papers.title: Tracing small-scale structure formation through cosmic time with strong gravitational lensing: A case for a next-generation sub-millimetre/millimetre interferometer
papers.abstract: The nature of dark matter and the growth of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remain major open questions in modern astrophysics. Both leave a key signature in an overlapping, largely unexplored mass range: $<10^7$ M$_{\odot}$ dark haloes and wandering black holes. These may be undetectable directly, but detectable through gravitational perturbation of strongly lensed images, and partly or entirely distinguishable from one another through lensing data alone. We demonstrate through realistic simulations that a 255-element sub-mm/mm interferometer could probe this critical mass regime, detecting gravitational perturbations in strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) from objects down to at least $10^5$ M$_{\odot}$. Combined with lens-galaxy characterisation from the European Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), which strengthens the physical interpretation of detected perturbers, and the unprecedented lens samples expected from Euclid and the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), this facility could deliver a census of low-mass dark matter haloes and wandering massive black holes across cosmic time.

papers.title: Binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution
papers.abstract: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHB) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. The dynamics and evolution of SMBHBs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. Many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec SMBHBs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. In a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying SMBHBs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. The caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. Each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. In this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (BLAST). We explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the SMBHB, and the relative inclination. Systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. In the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (QPLS), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. We determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their Fourier transforms. This study may help construct search pipelines to identify SMBHBs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.

papers.title: Analytical Time-Domain Waveforms for Black-Hole Scattering in the Self-Force Expansion
papers.abstract: We obtain a systematic understanding of the time-domain gravitational waveform of hyperbolic black-hole scattering at first order in the self-force expansion and all orders in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian (PN/PM) expansion. The continuous frequency spectrum of unbound orbits makes the inverse Fourier transform to the time domain diverge order by order; we introduce a dimensional-regularization-inspired prescription that cures this uniformly. We show that the full waveform then follows, at any PM and PN order, from a single family of integrals, generated by the Lauricella function $F_D^{(3)}$, which we calculate using strategies familiar from the study of Feynman integrals. As a proof of principle, we use this understanding to compute the quadrupolar 1SF waveform through relative 10PM-20PN, that is to order ${\cal O}(G^{10} v^{42})$, the full 1SF waveform to 10PM-10PN, as well as the asymptotic fluxes and the dissipative scattering angle at the corresponding accuracy.

papers.title: Thermalization of the Primordial Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background
papers.abstract: It is conventionally believed that the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background (SGWB) from inflation provides information about the earliest universe. However, in this Letter, we present a different picture. Our analysis starts from the observation that the inflation-predicted spectrum implies gravitons reside in high-occupation states, which significantly enhances their self-interactions and triggers rapid thermalization. We show that approximately $80\%$ of the primordial gravitons participate in this thermalization, forming a Bose--Einstein distribution and thereby erasing the primordial information. Evaluated using typical inflation parameters, this thermalized spectrum yields a present-day peak frequency of $f_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 1.4 \times 10^8 \, \mathrm{Hz}$ in the hundred-megahertz band with a peak amplitude of $Ω_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 3.5 \times 10^{-13}$. Due to the sharp drop-off away from the peak, the resulting spectrum lies beyond the reach of low-frequency observatories like PTAs, LISA, and LIGO, but remains uniquely accessible to high-frequency detectors such as microwave cavity resonators and dielectric haloscopes.

papers.title: Geometrical and Optical Design of the GUEST Laser-Ranged Test Masses for the Detection of Gravitational Waves in the $μ$Hz range
papers.abstract: The GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking) mission aims at detecting gravitational waves in the yet almost unexplored $μ$Hz frequency range through high-precision orbital tracking. The unprecedented scientific objectives of this experiment demand equally advanced optical solutions: the highly eccentric orbit imposes dual measurement regimes; a low-velocity, long-range scenario at apogee and a high-velocity, short-range scenario at perigee. The substantial disparity between these conditions is addressed through a novel optical architecture incorporating two distinct types of Corner-Cube Retroreflectors (CCRs) with 1" and 2" apertures (CCR1 and CCR2, respectively). The proposed layout has been designed to ensure isotropy and homogeneity of the optical response while maintaining efficient packing over the spherical surface of the spacecraft. The resulting Optical Cross-Section (OCS) has been evaluated using a custom reduced-order model, which captures the behavior of individual CCRs under varying illumination conditions. This model has been calibrated by reconstructing the optical response of the LARES-2 satellite and has enabled a detailed assessment of the contributions of each CCR type along the GUEST orbit. Finally, sensitivity analyses have been conducted to investigate the impact of key design parameters, including the ratio between CCR types, laser wavelength, spacecraft diameter, Dihedral Angle Offsets (DAOs), and mechanical configurations.

papers.title: Correlation between gravitational wave frequencies as a signature of new black hole physics
papers.abstract: We point out that for black holes (BH) of the same mass, despite of arising from two entirely different physical arguments, the peak frequency of the coarse-grained gravitational wave (GW) spectrum of gravitons $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}$ is very close to the peak frequency of the GW spectrum produced from binary BH mergers $f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}$. In particular, we find that $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}/f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}\approx 2.3$ independent from BH mass or population. If BHs are still evaporating, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{-1}$ with $M_i$ is the initial BH mass. If BHs evaporated in the radiation (matter) dominated era, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{1/2}$ ($\propto M_i$) respectively after taking into account redshift effect. Any deviation from the aforementioned magical ratio would indicate new BH physics. The sweetest frequency ballpark to look for this correlation is around $10^{14}\ \rm Hz-10^{20}\ \rm Hz$ where both GW spectra are allowed to have maximum amplitude. As a demonstration of what the new physics could be, we consider a phenomenological self-similar regular BH model of Hayward featuring a single hair parameter. The observed ratio of peak frequencies can be used to directly infer the hair parameter, along with crucial properties of the novel BH solution such as Hawking temperature, horizon size, and innermost stable circular orbit. We also comment on the pros and cons of correlating frequencies among other GW sources such as formation, population fluctuation, and sudden transition of adiabatic perturbation.

papers.title: Testing Charged Black Holes Embedded in Anisotropic Matter and Surrounded by Plasma through Gravitational Lensing: Bounds from the Sloan Lens ACS Survey
papers.abstract: We investigate weak gravitational lensing by a charged black hole surrounded by anisotropic matter, described by the two-component Kiselev metric, and immersed in a homogeneous plasma. We first examine the black hole geometry and horizon structure and then derive the weak-deflection angle from the Hamiltonian description of light propagation in plasma, using an expansion with a fixed turning point that we verify against direct numerical integration. Using the gravitational lens equation, we obtain the Einstein-ring angle, the image positions, the total magnification and the fractional magnifications of the primary and secondary images. We then confront the model with the Einstein radii of two galaxy-scale lenses of the Sloan Lens ACS Survey, J0008$-$0004 and J0029$-$0055. Because the Einstein angle cannot be smaller than the reduced deficit deflection, the observed radii give the mass-independent bounds $K<6.5\times10^{-6}$ and $K<4.2\times10^{-6}$, respectively. The charge correction to the Einstein radius is suppressed by $r_s/R_E\approx 5\times10^{-6}$ and is unobservable, while the plasma parameter at the optical wavelengths of the SLACS imaging is of order $10^{-22}$ and cannot be constrained. Our results show that galaxy-scale strong lensing data place stringent limits on anisotropic matter surrounding the lens, whereas plasma effects can be probed only at low radio frequencies.

papers.title: Quantum Field Theory Of Cosmological Perturbations Induced By Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The growth of primordial perturbations during the matter-dominated era is primarily driven by dark matter. Ultralight scalar fields (ULDM) are a promising candidate for this role, conventionally modeled as operating in a classical, high-occupation regime. In this work, we develop a first-principles field-theoretic framework to investigate the impact of ULDM on linear cosmological perturbations during matter domination, explicitly retaining its quantum nature. Deriving a closed equation for the graviton field dynamics, we compute and regularize its source terms for a generic Gaussian initial state of the ULDM field within the adiabatic (WKB) approximation, employing the middle-point working assumption for non-local terms. After gauge-fixing we find that, contrary to previous claims, the classical condensate of ULDM has no influence on gravitational wave propagation. However, the time-dependent graviton effective mass induced by quantum pressure of the squeezed state can drive parametric resonance in specific primordial gravitational wave modes. We demonstrate this growth is negligible for non-relativistic ULDM at matter-radiation equality under the assumption of a power-law squeezing spectrum for masses in the range $m \sim 10^{-21}{-}10^{-24}$ eV.

papers.title: Strong gravitational lensing with Euclid
papers.abstract: Euclid data is going to lead to the discovery of approximately 10^5 new strong gravitational lenses, thereby increasing the number of known lenses by a factor of 30. Such an impressive jump has the potential to revolutionise the field of strong lensing, by covering an ever-increasing range in the parameter space occupied by the lenses and lensed sources, and by uncovering rare and precious strong lens systems. The first quick data release of Euclid has already revealed hundreds of lenses, giving us a taste of what the final Euclid strong lens sample might look like. These lenses include a variety of objects acting as deflectors, from isolated galaxies to clusters, from early-type galaxies to edge-on disks. As many as four double-source plane lenses, in which one foreground object lenses two galaxies at two different redshifts, have already been discovered. As more data are acquired, it might become possible to detect the strong lensing signature of dwarf galaxy satellites, and to find lenses with an unusually large number of images. In this paper, we try to anticipate the kind of discoveries that these data will bring along.

papers.title: Cosmology with strong gravitational lenses
papers.abstract: Three of the most pressing open questions in cosmology -- the nature of dark energy and dark matter, and the growing tension in the value of the Hubble constant H$_0$ -- call for cosmological probes that are independent of, and complementary to, traditional methods. Strong gravitational lensing offers exactly that: a purely gravitational probe of the universe's expansion history and matter distribution, sensitive to dark matter's presence regardless of whether it interacts with light. Time-delay lenses and multiplane lenses can measure H$_0$ and the dark energy equation of state directly, while the distortion of lensed images can reveal the abundance and internal structure of dark matter subhalos. After a brief theoretical and historical introduction, I review recent breakthroughs enabled by JWST and by advances in lens modeling and stellar dynamics. Examples include the recent measurement of H$_0$ with 3\% precision in flat $Λ$ cold dark matter cosmology, and a tentative detection of dark matter self-interaction. Strong lensing is entering a pivotal era: wide-field surveys with Euclid, Rubin, and Roman, and radio surveys with the Square Kilometer Array, are poised to increase the number of known strong lenses by orders of magnitude, positioning strong lensing to play a central role in answering these open questions in the decade ahead.

papers.title: Pseudo-spectral methods in gravitational lensing: Spin precession in loop quantum black hole spacetimes
papers.abstract: Gravitational lensing is usually treated as an initial value problem: for a given impact parameter of an unbound orbit, one computes the resulting deflection angle. In this paper we advocate the inverse point of view. For a prescribed deflection angle, the orbit is selected by two boundary conditions at spatial infinity, so that the lensing problem becomes a well-defined two-point boundary value problem, with the impact parameter playing the role of a nonlinear eigenvalue. We show that pseudo-spectral methods based on Chebyshev collocation solve this boundary value problem accurately at modest computational cost, and that the parallel transport equations governing the spin precession of the particle reduce to a single linear system on the same grid. As a concrete application, we compute the spin precession of massive particles in backward scattering off two black hole spacetimes from loop quantum gravity: the covariant effective metric and the self-dual loop quantum black hole. All equations are written for a general static, spherically symmetric line element with three free functions, so that both spacetimes are handled on the same footing. We find that the quantum corrections are most pronounced for slowly moving particles, while in the ultra-relativistic limit the universal spin flip is always recovered. The flip itself is universal, but the rate at which it is approached is not: the derivative of $\cosξ$ with respect to the particle speed at $v=1$ is a strong-field quantity in every backward channel and depends clearly on the quantum parameters of both spacetimes. The framework is not restricted to the models studied here and applies to any static, spherically symmetric spacetime.

papers.title: Superhorizon enhancement of the hydrodynamic GW tail in Standard Model embedded warm inflation
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic fluctuations in the primordial plasma generate a gravitational-wave (GW) background that grows like $f^3_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ in terms of the current frequency. However, within the ($10^{-4}_{ } ... 10^4_{ })\,$Hz band of upcoming interferometers, the modes likely re-entered the Hubble horizon when the hydrodynamic noise was no longer at its maximal value. To address this situation, we define a model-independent transfer function for GWs generated by hydrodynamic (or other white-noise) fluctuations at any time. Employing appropriate variables, we show how this transfer function, together with the simpler vacuum one, can be determined numerically for a general expansion history. The results are illustrated for Standard Model embedded warm inflation scenarios, including both the vacuum and hydrodynamic parts. Following previous estimates, we find that a pre-exit-generated hydrodynamic tail becomes almost flat below $(10^5_{ } ... 10^7_{ })\;$Hz. Its small-$f^{ }_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ intercept remains finite, and can then moderately influence observational constraints through the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$).

papers.title: Isotensor $πππ$ scattering with a $ρ$ resonant subsystem from QCD
papers.abstract: This work presents a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) determination of $πππ$ scattering amplitudes for the isospin-2 channel with angular momentum and parity $J^{P} = 1^+$. The calculation is performed using unphysically heavy light-quark masses, corresponding to a pion mass of $m_π \approx 400$~MeV, for which the $ρ$ meson manifests as a narrow resonance. The analysis employs a previously developed formalism that non-perturbatively relates the finite-volume spectra of two- and three-pion systems to their infinite-volume scattering amplitudes. We combine earlier lattice QCD results for $ππ$ systems with isospins 1 and 2 with new determinations of the isospin-2 three-pion finite-volume spectrum, obtained for three cubic, periodic lattice volumes with box lengths ranging from $\approx 4/m_π$ to $6/m_π$. These combined data constrain the low-lying partial waves of the infinite-volume three-pion K matrix, from which we solve a set of coupled integral equations to extract the corresponding scattering amplitudes.

papers.title: Probing scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves in the nHz band: NANOGrav and SKA
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (PBH) physics. In addition to SIGWs, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (STGWs) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB). In this paper, we compute the STGWs generated during a generic matter-dominated (MD) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (eMD) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (RD) stage, working in the Poisson gauge. We find that, in a purely MD age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an eMD phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the eMD period. We then investigate whether the STGW signal could provide a dominant contribution to the \texttt{NANOGrav 15-year} dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). In particular, we consider STGWs generated during both eMD and RD eras, including their linear-order contributions. We further inject the scalar-induced contribution, both as an additional component and as the only signal, and compare the spectra against the same datasets. Our results show that, although the SIGWs still appear to provide the dominant contribution and the posteriors are tightly constrained by the requirement of avoiding PBH overproduction, the GWs induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive nano-Hz detectors of the SGWB.

papers.title: Nonoscillatory gravitational quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter spacetime
papers.abstract: We revisit quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter black holes, a classical and seemingly well-understood solution of Einstein-Maxwell theory with a positive cosmological constant. While previous studies have focused almost exclusively on the oscillatory photon-sphere branch, we show that two additional branches of nonoscillatory, purely imaginary modes - associated with the de Sitter horizon and with the regime of near-extremal charge (zero-damped) - are essential for a complete description of the spectrum. These modes have so far remained largely unexplored for gravitational perturbations despite their relevance for late-time dynamics and stability. In particular, we derive accurate analytic expressions for the purely imaginary quasinormal frequencies in the slow-damping regime, providing a complete description of this sector of the spectrum.

papers.title: Complex chromoelectric polarizability of a heavy-quarkonium resonance: pole response and channel-resolved effective-theory representation
papers.abstract: For a stable compact quarkonium state in the pNRQCD multipole regime, chromoelectric polarizability arises at leading order from two E1 transitions through virtual color-octet states. For an unstable state, we define the corresponding response through the quadratic displacement of its complex resonance pole in a weak chromoelectric background, so that its real and imaginary parts describe field-induced shifts of the pole mass and width. Starting from a renormalized background-field correlator, we show that the resonance polarizability is given by the complete two-field kernel normalized by the energy derivative of the full inverse propagator at the pole. In an effective theory with explicitly separated intermediate sectors, the kernel contains the standard E1-octet-E1 contribution, the complete source response of decay channels already coupled at zero field, and local contributions. This distinction becomes essential above open-flavor threshold and reduces to the standard pNRQCD polarizability in the stable, energy-independent limit. A simple $D\bar D$ realization for the $ψ(3770)$ gives the complex pole-residue factor $1/[1-σ'(z_ψ)]=0.800-0.336$, illustrating that threshold dressing can substantially modify both the magnitude and phase of the response. The resulting pole-based relation identifies the quantity required for a source-dependent coupled-channel determination of the chromoelectric polarizability of a heavy-quarkonium resonance.

papers.title: The WDM time-frequency transform in gravitational-wave data analysis II: Evolutionary spectrum and noise covariance
papers.abstract: Noise cannot be treated as stationary over the timescales required for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors, minutes for ground-based and months for space-based detectors. Nonstationarity leads to a non-diagonal frequency-domain noise covariance matrix, thus motivating a shift to the time-frequency domain. We introduce \emph{evolutionary power spectra} for describing nonstationary noise in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency basis. Under the framework of oscillatory processes, we show that, to leading order in the ratio of the Meyer filter and the nonstationarity timescales, the evolutionary spectrum is a power-frequency distribution that can be estimated from a single noise realization. We derive the corresponding noise covariance matrix and show that it is band tri-diagonal, like its stationary counterpart. The exact covariance to all orders is positive semi-definite by construction and dense depending on the noise. We further derive the optimal tiling of the time-frequency plane that minimizes the error of a diagonal covariance approximation and show that coarse-graining the plane suppresses correlations quadratically. Using simulated data with a LISA Galactic foreground and a drifting powerlaw spectrum, we show that the stationarity approximation leads to signal-to-noise ratio loss and severely biases inference. For realistic LISA data, approximating the covariance as diagonal in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer domain is accurate for the narrow-band analysis of a single resolved Galactic binary, but insufficient for a broad-band analysis. Finally, we provide mitigation strategies for the wraparound correlations induced across the data time edges whenever the spectrum differs between the start and the end of the data.

papers.title: Strong-Field Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Ray-Traced Arrival-Time Surfaces
papers.abstract: The diffraction integral formalism has been greatly successful in describing gravitational wave lensing effects in scenarios where the wavelength of the signal is comparable to the characteristic length scale of the lens, known as the wave optics regime. However, the assumptions required to construct its integrand break down as the source approaches the strong gravity region of a black hole lens. In particular, we are interested in the lensed signal from a binary (the source) near a massive black hole (the lens). We present a new formalism for obtaining low frequency corrections to sources being lensed in the strong field regime of gravity by leveraging the fact that null geodesics obey the Hamilton--Jacobi equations. In doing so, we are able to construct a time delay surface without relying on the thin lens approximation, and solve the diffraction integral for the resulting surface directly. For a stationary source at $10M$, deep in the strong field regime, when comparing the results with a relativistic wave scattering model, we find $6.5\%$ and $0.3\%$ agreement in the peak amplification and first diffractive fringe, respectively. Furthermore, we find a $< 1\%$ agreement with the amplitude of the point mass lens with a source at $10^4 M$ in the weak field, but noticeable dephasing between the peaks of the amplification function at higher frequencies. This work allows for clean interpolation between otherwise separate regimes, valid for sources from $\sim 6M \to \infty$. It provides a transparent, physically motivated framework for computing beyond-geometric optics lensing effects in the strong field regime.

papers.title: Audible curvaton: modulated phase transition as the origin of large-scale curvature perturbations and gravitational wave anisotropies
papers.abstract: We propose a post-inflationary first-order phase transition modulated by a light spectator field as the origin of primordial large-scale curvature perturbations. Spectator fluctuations acquired during inflation modulate the bubble nucleation history, generating curvature perturbations together with correlated intrinsic gravitational-wave (GW) anisotropies. We show that this mechanism can reproduce the observed amplitude of curvature perturbations while producing a loud stochastic GW background in the frequency bands of space-based detectors such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin. A concrete benchmark yields strongly enhanced intrinsic GW anisotropies and a local primordial non-Gaussianity signal within reach of future large-scale-structure surveys.

papers.title: Spinformation: do gravitational-wave events carry information beyond effective spins?
papers.abstract: While the spin vectors of binary black holes offer insight into the astrophysical formation channels of these systems, individual spins are less precisely measured through gravitational-wave observations than the effective inspiral spin $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and the effective precession spin $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Reducing to effective parameters discards information in the data, but how much information is lost has yet to be demonstrated. Here we show how to quantify whether individual mergers carry information about component spins beyond the constraints implied by effective parameters (a.k.a. spinformation) and apply the technique to GWTC-5. Thresholding on information loss $\gtrsim 0.25$ bits, over $80\%$ of gravitational-wave events in GWTC-5 have component spin posteriors described by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ alone. Only $\sim3\%$ of gravitational-wave events have substantial spin information not explained by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. The catalog's component spin information is effectively two-dimensional in $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Using simulated signals, we find the noise realization can create or destroy over a bit of beyond-$χ_\mathrm{eff}$ information: the structure in real data may therefore be driven by noise. At current sensitivity, component spins provide interpretive\textemdash rather than informational\textemdash advantage over effective parameters.

papers.title: Identity Crisis: Untangling Mass-Ordering Artifacts from Compact-Object Pairing in Gravitational-Wave Populations
papers.abstract: Mass distributions of binary black hole mergers inferred from gravitational-wave observations offer clues to how binaries form. These distributions conventionally label the heavier component as the primary, with mass $m_1$, and the lighter as the secondary, with mass $m_2$, such that $m_1 \geq m_2$. This ordering folds the physically labeled mass distribution along the equal-mass line, potentially reshaping the underlying population structure. In this Letter, we determine which population features can arise from mass ordering and which require genuine astrophysical structure. We show that ordering alone can produce (1) an $m_2$ distribution that declines more rapidly than the $m_1$ distribution, without intrinsic differences between the physically labeled components, and (2) an apparent concentration along equal masses, without correlations that preferentially pair black holes of equal mass. Moreover, different physically labeled populations can produce the same ordered mass distribution. Crucially, however, a preferred companion mass that remains constant as $m_1$ increases requires a characteristic mass scale already present in the physically labeled population. Applied to binary black hole mergers in the fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, our model recovers such a scale near $m_2 \simeq 50\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. Around this scale, the merger-rate density declines much more rapidly toward higher $m_2$ than toward lower $m_2$, ruling out an equal or weaker high-$m_2$ decline at 99.45% credibility. This structure therefore requires a characteristic mass scale in at least one physically labeled component, but masses alone cannot determine which component carries it. Any formation model reproducing the observed high-mass binary black hole merger population must contain such a scale.

papers.title: Late-time electric screening in dS from EAdS loops
papers.abstract: We compute the one-loop gauge-field two-point functions analytically in scalar QED on dS$_{d+1}$ for general dimension and scalar mass, using the EAdS reformulation of the in-in formalism arXiv:2007.09993. The Dirichlet EAdS gauge field acquires a Schwinger-type mass, with its longitudinal mode supplied by a composite of charged scalars obeying opposite boundary conditions, while the Neumann mode remains protected by gauge invariance. In dS, the Dirichlet correction induces an anomalous dimension $γ_J$ for the boundary current and modifies the late-time falloff of the electric field. This bulk calculation reproduces the boundary multiplet-recombination result of arXiv:2509.18888. Summing over the in-in contour branches gives the retarded dS bubble kernel, making direct contact with the Bros-Moschella framework. We establish a spectral Cutkosky rule that expresses the discontinuity of this kernel across the principal-series cut in the Casimir plane in terms of a two-particle cut, with both internal scalar lines placed on shell. Although the full bubble coefficient involves a ${}_7F_6$ hypergeometric function, the cut collapses to a closed product of Gamma functions and determines the complete non-local part of the kernel through a dispersion relation. Analytic continuation of the same cut reproduces the complete one-loop result for $γ_J$. In the complex Casimir plane, the loop-corrected Dirichlet photon appears as a pole on the second sheet and is therefore naturally interpreted as a dS resonance, or quasinormal mode, whose frequency is shifted at one loop.

papers.title: Resonant photon-axion conversion driven by axion dark matter oscillations
papers.abstract: Wave propagation in periodically time-dependent media can exhibit driven mode conversion that is absent in static or adiabatic descriptions. We show that coherent axion dark matter provides an intrinsic realization of this dynamics for photons propagating in a magnetic field. The background's periodic birefringence continuously rotates the photon polarization and thereby drives magnetic photon--axion mixing. Using Floquet theory, we derive resonant photon--axion conversion when integer harmonics of the axion oscillation frequency compensate the dispersion mismatch, $Δ_γ-Δ_a\approx n m_a$ with $n\in\mathbb{Z}$. This resonance enables efficient mixing far from conventional level crossing and is lost when the periodic drive is averaged out of the propagation Hamiltonian. The resulting conversion is bounded and unitary, distinct from parametric instability or axion decay. Our framework describes photon propagation in coherent oscillating axion backgrounds and predicts characteristic polarization signatures, which we illustrate in a blazar environment.

papers.title: Tidal Excitation of Relativistic Stars
papers.abstract: How a relativistic star responds to a time-dependent tide has lacked a first-principles counterpart of the Newtonian normal-mode expansion. In general relativity, the tidal field is gauge sensitive, radiative modes are non-Hermitian and incomplete, and the direct and late-time responses are intrinsically nonmodal. In this work we present, to our knowledge, the first causal relativistic theory that treats all of these components on equal footing. We first develop the spectral decomposition of the retarded Green function of the matched stellar interior--Schwarzschild exterior, which classifies four separate regimes in time domain: acausal region, prompt wave, surface-reflected wave, and mode+tail. The prompt signal is identical to that of a Schwarzschild black hole with the same mass, which is combined with the surface-reflected wave to be referred as the "direct part". With the Green function and a complex bilinear form on the full metric--fluid phase space, we decompose the linear response of a nonrotating perfect-fluid star into direct, quasinormal-mode, and late-time-tail sectors. Crucially, every sector admits an explicit first-order driven evolution equation: discrete bilinear projections determine the dynamically evolving quasinormal-mode amplitudes, while continuum projections of the same tidal source onto branch-cut states determine the direct and tail amplitudes. The result is a complete modal--nonmodal decomposition of the spacetime and fluid perturbations, which is physically described by the dynamics of a discrete and a continuous-frequency set of oscillators. We verify the decomposition numerically under generic time-dependent tidal driving and discuss applications to black hole perturbations.

papers.title: Constraints on the cosmic reheating history from PTA data
papers.abstract: The cosmic reheating is an important epoch in the very early Universe, and has significant impacts on the primordial black hole (PBH) abundance and the scalar-induced gravitational wave (SIGW) spectrum. The relevant energy scale and the constituents of cosmic medium are encoded in the reheating frequency $f_{\mathrm{reh}}$ and the equation of state parameter $w$. In this work, we perform a full parameter space Bayesian inference, using the NANOGrav 15-yr dataset to constrain the thermal history of reheating. Treating $f_{\mathrm{reh}}$ and $w$ as free parameters, we systematically investigate the Dirac $δ$, narrow and broad log-normal primordial power spectra. Current pulsar timing array data can effectively constrain the peak frequency of the SIGW spectrum as $f_{\rm p}\sim 10^{-7.6}$--$10^{-7.0}$ Hz, along with $f_{\rm reh}\sim 10^{-9.0}$--$10^{-8.3}$ Hz and $w\sim 0.19$--$0.79$ (the $68\%$ confidence level), when the power spectrum has a relatively narrow width $Δ\lesssim 1$. A broader power spectrum introduces a smoothing effect that obscures the characteristic frequency knee in the SIGW spectrum, leading to the loss of information about cosmic reheating. Furthermore, for the Dirac $δ$ and narrow spectra, the PBH masses associated with the SIGWs are anchored at the planetary mass scale around $10^{-6}$--$10^{-4} M_{\odot}$. This establishes a consistent physical framework that naturally bridges the nanohertz gravitational wave background with the dark matter candidates implied by the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment microlensing events.

papers.title: Bilinear products and the orthogonality of quasinormal modes on hyperboloidal foliations
papers.abstract: We explore the properties of bilinear products for black-hole quasinormal modes (QNMs) formulated on hyperboloidal foliations. We find that, although QNM solutions are smooth and finite on future-directed hyperboloids, the integrand of the bilinear form with respect to which the modes are orthogonal is still divergent. This is a result of the reflection (equivalently, CPT) transformation required in the definition of the products, which modifies the behaviour of the integrand at the boundaries. We present several regularisation procedures that yield a finite and well-defined bilinear form. In addition, we examine an alternative definition of the bilinear products that incorporates flux contributions, discussing its advantages and limitations. Finally, we define the QNM excitation factors and coefficients within the hyperboloidal framework in terms of the bilinear products, and compute them explicitly for a choice of mode numbers and constant initial data. For concreteness, we work with the QNMs associated to scalar perturbations of the Schwarzschild family of spacetimes.

papers.title: Signature of GW from the Hidden Sector in light of the Recent LZ Event
papers.abstract: The LZ collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear-recoil event at $E_R=248\pm23_\text{stat}\pm23_\text{sys}$ keV, observed in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure with a local significance of $3.4σ$, pointing towards an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation. We explain this event within a gauged $U(1)_X$ hidden-sector model, spontaneously broken by a singlet scalar whose vacuum expectation value (VEV) gives rise to: \textit{(i)} gauge boson mass, \textit{(ii)} a small Majorana mass for the vector-like singlet fermion, the DM candidate, charged under the new symmetry, which splits the fermion into two pseudo-Dirac states (mass splitting proportional to the scalar VEV) thus resulting in a purely off-diagonal vector current, \textit{(iii)} the frequency and the amplitude of the GW signal arising from the hidden sector symmetry breaking via first-order phase transition (FOPT). The symmetry-breaking scale thus provides a multi-messenger probe connecting terrestrial direct-detection kinematics at the LZ and early-universe FOPT thermodynamics while obtaining thermal DM relic abundance. We delineate the viable parameter space compatible with the LZ event, correct relic density, and detectable GW signals in the low frequency regimes at future interferometers like $μ{\rm ARES}$ and THEIA while satisfying existing cosmological, astrophysical, and terrestrial bounds.

papers.title: Scalar-induced gravitational waves from a box-shaped curvature power spectrum
papers.abstract: We compute the stochastic background of gravitational waves (GWs) produced at second order in cosmological perturbation theory by a primordial curvature power spectrum that is flat in $\ln k$ over a finite band $[k_-,k_+]=[k_*e^{-Δ},k_*e^{+Δ}]$ and vanishes elsewhere. This logarithmic box interpolates between a monochromatic spectrum as $Δ\to0$ and a locally scale-invariant plateau as $Δ\to\infty$, and its sharp boundaries make the geometry of the source convolution unusually transparent. Working in the radiation era, we reduce the convolution to a compact integral over the overlap between the momentum triangle and the box, and evaluate it analytically in two regimes. For a narrow box we show that, to leading order in the width, the spectrum equals the Dirac-spectrum result multiplied by a purely geometric overlap factor $Φ_{\rm box}(κ,Δ)$; this factor turns the infrared slope from $k^{3}\ln^{2}k$ into $k^{2}\ln^{2}k$ at a break $k_b=2k_*\sinhΔ$. For a broad box we separate the lower edge, the scale-invariant interior, and the upper edge, derive the leading behaviour in each (an infrared $k^{3}\ln^{2}k$ rise, a scale-invariant plateau, and a quartic cut-off at the hard endpoint $k=2k_+$), and combine them into a single uniform formula cast as a product of two universal, $Δ$-independent edge functions. We also provide an integral-free closed-form surrogate for these edge functions for use in parameter scans.

papers.title: The Promise of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
papers.abstract: We review the promise of upcoming gravitational-wave (GW) observations in addressing some of the important open questions in astrophysics and cosmology. A decade after the first direct detection of GWs, the field is entering a transformative phase driven by progressive detector upgrades and the anticipated advent of space-based and next-generation ground-based observatories. These instruments will not only push the distance horizon of GW observations to cosmological redshifts, but will dramatically extend the accessible frequency band, opening entirely new source classes that lie beyond the reach of current detectors. The source landscape is rich enough that surprises are likely. This review surveys our current understanding across this landscape and offers some perspective on the discoveries that upcoming GW observations are poised to deliver.

papers.title: Resonant JPZ algebras and 3D Chern--Simons gravity
papers.abstract: In this work we construct three-dimensional Chern--Simons gravity theories for the six resonant $JPZ$ algebras generated by the Lorentz generators $J_a$, translations $P_a$, and an additional Lorentz-like generator $Z_a$. The resonance condition together with the Jacobi identities leaves precisely six configurations arising from the semigroup expansions. Our main result is that three of them, $B_4$, $\widetilde C_4$, and $C_4$, are isomorphic to $iso(2,1)\oplus so(2,1)$, although they yield different gravitational realizations when we keep the original $JPZ$ field identification fixed. For each case $JPZ$, we determine the invariant tensors, gauge curvatures, Chern--Simons action, field equations, and the corresponding maximal-rank coupling sectors. The field equations can be written in the compact form $Ω_σ\mathbf F=0$, which makes explicit how the additional field $h^a$ contributes to the curvature, torsion, and the remaining gauge-curvature components. We use the direct-sum isomorphisms to classify the local metric sectors and to relate them to known global and asymptotic solutions, while keeping the gravitational interpretation tied to the original $(ω,e,h)$ fields.

papers.title: MRI Turbulence versus $α$-Viscosity in Circumbinary Disks: Implications for Gravitational-Wave Dephasing and Accretion Variability
papers.abstract: Our understanding of gas torques on massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) relies on hydrodynamical (HD) simulations of circumbinary disks (CBDs) in which an $α$-viscosity models angular momentum transport. However, CBDs around MBHBs near merger are hot, magnetized plasmas where transport is driven by magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) turbulence sustained by the magnetorotational instability (MRI). We test how well an $α$-viscosity captures MRI turbulence with 3D global Athena++ simulations of a locally isothermal CBD around an equal-mass, circular MBHB, run in HD and MHD from the same initial torus on identical grids, so that only the transport mechanism differs. Excising the region within twice the binary separation, $r<2~a_{\rm bin}$, allows $1000$ orbits of evolution, several times longer than previous MHD simulations. Both disks deliver the same accretion rate, and the gas beyond $2~a_{\rm bin}$ exerts a positive torque in both, yet the MHD torque is $3.5$ times larger and $3$ times more variable. Near the midplane, transport is similar in the disk body but three times weaker in MHD at the cavity edge, where $2$-$3$ times more mass piles up in a more eccentric cavity, raising the torque. The accretion rate is modulated mainly at twice the binary frequency in HD, but by a persistent lump at the cavity edge and its beat with the binary in MHD. The outer-disk torque therefore implies a contribution to the gas-induced phase shift in the gravitational-wave signal of LISA binaries $3.5$ times larger than in $α$-disk models, and a different variability signature for LSST and Roman.

papers.title: Massive Graviton Dark Matter from a Gapped Continuum
papers.abstract: We consider the possibility of dark matter in a warped extra-dimensional theory in the presence of a linear dilaton background, with a gapped continuum spectrum, in a brane-world cosmological scenario. Firstly, triggered by self-energy radiative corrections, we study the existence of an isolated resonance of massive gravitons, and its realization as a long-lived feebly interacting dark matter candidate, produced by the freeze-in mechanism. This massive graviton is proved to satisfy all theoretical and experimental constraints, in the sub-MeV mass range. We further consider the close relationship between the existence of this component of dark matter and the presence of an inflaton localized on the brane, with a mass around $10^{11}$ GeV and a sub-TeV reheating temperature, in a brane inflationary scenario that allows one to reproduce the most recent cosmological observables. Secondly, the gapped continuum of gravitons, a particular five-dimensional realization of the physics of unparticles, is identified as a holographic fluid which can play the role of holographic dark matter. The production of the holographic fluid goes by an ultraviolet freeze-in mechanism, with an abundance mainly depending on the reheating temperature. Depending on the values of the mass gap and the reheating temperature, one or both components of dark matter can be present.

papers.title: Intermediate States in Chaotic Triple Evolution and Applications to Black Hole Merger Statistics
papers.abstract: Three-body interactions exhibit phases of strong chaotic evolution as well as hierarchical motion where one body separates from a binary and follows a hyperbolic or elliptic trajectory around it. The binaries produced during phases of hierarchical motion may lead to gravitational wave (GW) inspirals, but this depends on the outcomes of the chaotic states. In this paper we re-derive the elliptic outcome distribution using equilibrium statistical mechanics and explore it together with the hyperbolic distribution. When comparing to N-body simulations, we find that we can reduce the elliptic outcome model to one free parameter instead of the previously used two and that the predicted disintegration probabilities agree except for very low angular momentum triples. We then use both outcome distributions along with a star cluster model to design a Monte Carlo algorithm for repeated binary-single scatterings within dense star systems. We explore star cluster masses of $[10^5 - 10^7] M_{\odot}$, with the goal of quantifying observably eccentric merger (OEM) GWs, visible to instruments such as LIGO and Virgo. Assuming an OEM detection sensitivity of $f_{\rm min}=10 {\rm Hz}, e_{\rm min} = 0.1$, we find the elliptic OEMs are about $\sim (32 - 63)\%$ of the total elliptic mergers and that the total cluster mass greatly impacts the fraction of ejected binaries. The OEM to total merger fraction (OEM fraction) is found to be $(2.6 - 4.4)\%$. Considering the detection sensitivity that GW interferometers have today $(f_{\rm min} \simeq 34.4 {\rm Hz})$ we obtain the OEM fraction in the $(1.6 - 3.1)\%$ range.

papers.title: Analog regular black holes and black hole mimickers for surface-gravity waves in fluids
papers.abstract: Recent advances in the observation of black-hole candidates have renewed interest in probing their near-horizon structure and in searching for departures from the standard singular solutions of general relativity. In this context, significant effort has been devoted to regular black holes and to horizonless black-hole mimickers, motivated primarily by quantum-gravitational effects. Depending on the value of the regularization parameter relative to the object mass, typical spherically symmetric solutions can describe either of these two scenarios. Regular black-hole configurations generically feature an outer and an inner horizon surrounding a maximally symmetric core; the inner horizon in turn triggers mass inflation and semiclassical instabilities. The horizonless branch of the same solutions, by contrast, supports stable inner light rings when sufficiently compact, yet is itself subject to instabilities associated with long-lived quasinormal modes. Here we investigate how to emulate these spacetimes in an analogue-gravity platform based on surface-gravity waves in a shallow-water basin, with the aim of reproducing these instabilities experimentally. We begin by identifying the flow profiles and boundary conditions required to replicate the relevant effective geometries. In particular, we show that the inner-core metrics can be simulated with a non-rotating central-drainage configuration, and we propose a graded-drainage profile to connect them to an asymptotically flat exterior region. We then assess the experimental feasibility of studying the instabilities mentioned above with current technology. Our conclusion is that, while the required setup is realizable in principle, alternative media, such as Bose-Einstein condensates, may offer a more practical route to faithfully capturing the targeted physical features.

papers.title: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography
papers.abstract: Finite boundary drives ending at the same charge density can select different relaxation channels. We demonstrate this in a probe Abelian--Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane with a stable normal endpoint. Charge exchange during preparation modifies scalar propagation and source coupling. Density history and radial Maxwell feedback during and after the drive leave a cubic slow amplitude even after linear slow-mode cancellation. For the tested protocols at $ρ_f=3$, the density-history term interferes constructively with the net radial feedback; its modulus is 85--89\% of that of the total cubic coefficient. Calculated from the low-order equations alone, this total coefficient predicts the compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms the reduction from $O(ε^3)$ to $O(ε^5)$ in the source amplitude $ε$, with approximately 600-fold suppression for the representative protocol at $ε=0.05$. Compensation extends the window of fast-channel relaxation without changing the final quasinormal-mode spectrum; early distance crossing already arises from linear interference. Fully tuned two- and three-pulse preparations suppress one and two slow modes, respectively, within numerical resolution. Local analysis establishes finite-pulse reachability of strong Mpemba states with vanishing selected asymptotic slow-mode coefficients. Charge-neutral controls retain a total-time advantage from a common input when the full subsequent control duration is included.

papers.title: Self-stimulated avalanche in superradiant axion clouds
papers.abstract: Boson clouds formed via superradiance around spinning black holes offer a novel probe of ultralight particles. We show that such gravitational atoms can undergo a self-stimulated avalanche: a coherent quadrupolar transition is seeded by external gravitational waves and amplified by self-generated radiation feedback. We formulate an effective two-level description that captures the logistic population transfer and the resulting delayed gravitational-wave pulse with a characteristic envelope. This cooperative emission mechanism opens a new observational avenue into the ultralight dark sector.

papers.title: Pulse Morphology and Spectral Study of LPT J1634+44 Using GMRT
papers.abstract: Long-period radio transients (LPTs) are a recently discovered class of Galactic coherent radio emitters characterized by rotation periods of minutes to hours and highly polarized radio pulses. Their nature remains uncertain, with proposed scenarios invoking isolated or binary systems containing neutron stars (NSs) or white dwarfs (WDs). We investigate the nature of CHIME/ILT J1634+44 through multi-band observations with the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT), examining its pulse morphology, spectral evolution, and timing behavior. The pulses show substantial profile variability, and the subpulse features evolve significantly across observing frequencies. Using our measurements of quasi-periodic microstructures in J1634+44 pulses as well as those of other LPTs available from literature, we show that the scaling relationship between the rotation and microstructure periods is not limited to only neutron stars but extend to white dwarfs as well. The radio spectrum of J1634+44 is highly variable and exhibits a spectral turnover that shifts toward lower frequencies across observing epochs. Interpreting this turnover as free-free absorption, we constrain the physical properties of the intervening absorbing medium. Complementing these emission diagnostics, we also present analysis of pulse arrival times spanning approximately a decade to probe the previously proposed spin-orbit resonance models for this LPT.

papers.title: Late-time distance consistency and model-independent curvature inference with strong lensing, quasars, and galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: We revisit a late-time, model-independent distance-consistency framework that combines strong gravitational lensing systems (SGLS), ultraviolet/X-ray quasars (QSOs), and 38 Sunyaev--Zel'dovich/X-ray galaxy-cluster angular-diameter distances. The analysis focuses on systematics rather than on presenting a competitive curvature measurement. Starting from the 158-system SGLS catalog, we exclude 30 systems that violate the lensing-geometric requirement $D_{A,ls}/D_{A,s}<1$ in the isothermal reference case $γ_{\rm lens}=2$, leaving a fixed 128-system SGLS parent sample for cross-matching with 1598 QSOs. A deterministic maximum-cardinality, minimum-mismatch one-to-one assignment yields 100 SGLS--QSO pairs at the nominal $Δd/d=5\%$ threshold. We propagate the measured X-ray flux uncertainties and the intrinsic QSO scatter, and, crucially, we include the full $38\times38$ covariance induced by using the same QSO distances in the kernel-smoothed cluster predictions. With $Ω_K\sim\mathcal{U}[-10,10]$, the joint posterior is $Ω_K=2.085^{+1.634}_{-1.103}$ (68\%; central 95\% interval $[0.269,6.028]$). We do not interpret the positive shift as evidence for an open Universe. \added{This positive posterior offset is driven by cross-probe calibration tensions, sample-assignment effects, and the cluster anchor; it cannot be attributed to the intrinsic spatial geometry of the Universe.} The SGLS+QSO data alone leave curvature essentially prior dominated, $Ω_K=0.70^{+6.33}_{-7.12}$, whereas removing only the off-diagonal cluster covariance moves the posterior to $Ω_K=5.21^{+2.46}_{-2.07}$. Thus the cluster anchor supplies most of the curvature constraining power and its covariance materially changes the posterior location.

papers.title: Probing an Intermediate-Mass Black Hole Companion of Sagittarius A* with Pulsar Timing
papers.abstract: An intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) hidden in our Galactic Center (GC) may explain the puzzling observations of the stellar distribution around Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*), the supermassive black hole (SMBH) in the GC. Future observations with the next-generation radio telescopes, such as the SKA, are promising to discover pulsars orbiting around Sgr A*, and thus provide the possibility of constraining the hidden IMBH with pulsar timing. We study the detectability of a third-body, the IMBH, in the pulsar-SMBH system based on radio timing observation. We find that the pulsar-SMBH system is very sensitive to such a third-body perturbation and can be used to put stringent constraints on the existence of the IMBH. Even under strong perturbations caused by the complex GC astrophysical environments, timing observation will still complement the existing observational constraints.

papers.title: Robustness of Neural Networks for CMB Polarization Foreground Removal
papers.abstract: The detection of Cosmic Microwave Background primordial $B$-mode polarization would constitute a ``smoking gun" signal of primordial gravitational waves. However, this measurement requires accurate removal of polarized Galactic foregrounds to avoid systematic biases when estimating the tensor-to-scalar ratio. Methods based on Machine Learning techniques (ML), such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have recently been proposed as alternative foreground cleaning techniques, but their applicability to real data relies on their ability to generalize beyond the models assumed during training. In this work, we focus on a variety of foreground models (FMs) used for training and conduct a systematic study of the generalization properties of a CNN-based method. We train various CNN architectures on simulations generated from different Galactic FMs, and test their performance on models not used during the training. By characterizing the statistical properties of the FMs using variance, skewness, and Shannon entropy, we define a statistical complexity hierarchy among them. We show that training on the more complex FMs reduces bias and improves precision when testing on unseen FMs, whereas training on the simplest model could introduce systematic errors. These results evidence that a lack of generalization is a relevant source of systematic uncertainty, and emphasize the importance of understanding the impact of the models assumed during training in ML-based methods before applying them to real data.

papers.title: Testing the isothermal Jeans model for self-interacting dark matter halos in the collapse phase
papers.abstract: We benchmark the semi-analytical isothermal Jeans model against a high-resolution isolated N-body simulation that follows a self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halo into deep core collapse. The model accurately reproduces the density evolution through much of the collapse phase, although it does not capture the sharp rise in central velocity dispersion during collapse. When applied to strong gravitational lensing observables, such as the projected mass and logarithmic density slope of SIDM halos, the Jeans model tracks the simulated evolution more closely than the parametric approach in the deep collapse regime. Our results demonstrate that the isothermal Jeans model provides a reliable and computationally efficient description of SIDM halo evolution.

papers.title: Statistical Analysis of Neutron Star Cooling: Implications for the Nuclear Equation of State and Nucleon Pairing
papers.abstract: We perform a statistical analysis of the thermal evolution of isolated neutron stars by confronting theoretical cooling curves with luminosity-age measurements for 24 sources. For each object, we explore five purely nucleonic equations of state (APR4, FSU2R, DD2, IST, and NL3$ωρ$) combined with representative models of neutron superfluidity and proton superconductivity, while varying the gravitational mass and envelope composition. The analysis spans approximately $10^5$ cooling curves. Within this framework, we find that only the NL3$ωρ$ equation of state and, to a lesser extent, IST, both including neutron triplet pairing, provide an overall satisfactory description of the data. The remaining equations of state are in significant tension with the observations. These results demonstrate that NS cooling provides complementary constraints on dense matter, alongside nuclear structure, global NS observables, and gravitational-wave observations, while probing the interplay between the EoS and nucleon pairing.

papers.title: Cosmological pole-skipping, shock waves and quantum chaotic dynamics of de Sitter horizons
papers.abstract: We present a systematic analysis of pole-skipping for scalar, Maxwell, and gravitational waves in cosmological spacetimes. Specifically, working in empty de Sitter space and in Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole geometries, we locate the tower of pole-skipping points of such fields and show that they impose nontrivial constraints on the corresponding bulk two-point functions. Focusing on the gravitational sound channel, we then extract the Lyapunov exponent and butterfly velocities that characterize hypothetical dual many-body quantum chaos at each horizon. These chaotic data precisely match the outcome of a gravitational shock wave calculation, confirming that the relevant pole-skipping points encode high-energy scattering of horizon quanta. Interestingly, the butterfly velocities can become superluminal or imaginary, with the latter signaling a spatially modulated propagation of chaos. Assuming that a holographic dual exists, we translate our results into field theory language and propose that the dual theory can be divided into two entangled sectors that capture the black hole and cosmological horizon degrees of freedom. Our results suggest that the black hole sector becomes increasingly nonlocal as the black hole shrinks and that the cosmological horizon sector exhibits behavior compatible with violations of Hermiticity. Finally, we outline simple microscopic toy models, built from long-range and non-Hermitian deformations of the Double Scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (DSSYK)-type chains, that realize these features, providing a concrete arena for future exploration.

papers.title: $Δ(1232)$ isobars and weak-interaction bulk viscosity in neutron-star merger matter
papers.abstract: Binary neutron star mergers probe nuclear matter at densities of a few times nuclear saturation density and temperatures of tens of MeV, conditions under which heavier baryons such as the $Δ(1232)$ isobars may appear. Previous calculations of the bulk viscosity of merger matter have considered nucleonic matter, with and without muons, and hyperonic matter, but not $Δ$ isobars. In this work, we extend these calculations to neutrino-transparent matter in which $Δ$ isobars are present in strong equilibrium. We derive the relativistic matrix elements for the charged-current $Δ\to N$ and $Δ\toΔ'$ transitions, evaluate all electronic and muonic Urca processes over the full phase space using the nucleon width approximation, and include the in-medium $Δ\to Nπ$ width with Pauli blocking. The bulk viscosity is obtained from the coupled linear response of the electron and muon fractions about the finite-temperature flavor equilibrium. We find that the $Δ^-$ takes over the negative charge from the leptons, which raises the proton fraction and opens the nucleonic direct Urca process. Up to about 3~MeV this change in composition, rather than the $Δ$ reactions themselves, controls flavor equilibration. As a consequence, the resonant maximum of the bulk viscosity moves to lower temperatures for all oscillation frequencies we consider, and kHz density oscillations near resonance are damped several times faster than in nucleonic matter.
