We show that the saturated drift velocity, which falls below the Alfvén speed, can be accurately predicted from the wave spectra alone. If the CR distribution is undersampled, a numerical instability corrupts the largest resonant scales: unphysical, unresolved pitch-angle gradients resonantly generate backward-propagating waves, driving an inverse cascade that should be absent from purely streaming-driven waves. While power-law CR distributions may permit stronger NLLD, our results indicate that NLLD is unlikely to be an intrinsic saturation mechanism of the streaming instability; instead, its effectiveness hinges on the interplay of streaming-generated modes with those of external origin.

papers.title: The Impact of High-Mass Clusters on the Binary Black Hole Merger Rate over Cosmic Time
papers.abstract: We present a cosmological calculation of the binary black hole merger rate from dense star clusters, using a $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ ($\texttt{CMC}$) model grid spanning the full observed parameter space of cluster mass, metallicity, and virial radius. For the first time, we incorporate $N=10^{7}$-particle $\texttt{CMC}$ models into this calculation, including a new solar-metallicity model, extending the $\texttt{CMC Cluster Catalog}$ to the most massive clusters observed in the local Universe. Using an analytic cluster formation model which convolves the cluster formation rate with delay-time distributions from our model suite, we find that the local cluster BBH merger rate is dominated by low-mass ($M_1 \lesssim 20\,M_\odot$) mergers originating from recently formed, high-metallicity clusters. While high-mass clusters are the primary sites of hierarchical (second-generation and higher) mergers, their contribution to the overall merger rate is suppressed by the exponential cutoff of the cluster initial mass function. The hierarchical merger rate is therefore highly sensitive to the exact value of the Schechter mass, $M_S$, suggesting that gravitational wave constraints on the hierarchical merger fraction can independently constrain the high-mass end of the cluster initial mass function. Our cluster formation model reproduces the observed present-day GC number density without fine tuning, and we find $M_S = 10^7\,M_\odot$ provides the best match to the observed Virgo GC mass distribution. For this value, $27\%$ of local dynamical mergers are hierarchical, compared to $18\%$ for the canonical value of $M_S = 10^{6.26}\,M_\odot$. Our merger weights, which we make publicly available, can be used for direct comparison with LVK distributions and other formation models.

papers.title: Constraining the Progenitor Orbits of Sequential Black-Hole Mergers in Hierarchical Triples: Peters-Based Estimates
papers.abstract: Two black-hole merger events may originate from sequential mergers in a pre-existing hierarchical black-hole triple if their spatial localizations overlap and the remnant mass of the first merger is compatible with a component mass of the second. In this scenario, the inner binary merges first, leaving a remnant that remains bound to the tertiary and subsequently undergoes a second merger. We present a method to constrain the progenitor triple's outer orbit by modeling the gravitational-wave-driven evolution of the remnant-tertiary binary using Peters' equations. Given an assumed upper bound on the recoil velocity of the first merger, the method requires only the black-hole masses, the time delay between the mergers, and the eccentricity at a reference frequency - quantities that can be inferred from the merger events themselves. We investigate the potential constraining power by constructing a constraint atlas spanning a range of system properties and identify the conditions under which the method places tight and reliable bounds on the progenitor triple's outer orbital parameters. By imposing an upper bound on the detector-band eccentricity, we also obtain meaningful constraints for candidate hierarchical mergers proposed in the literature, including GW190514-GW190521. We provide numerical tools for applying the method to user-specified systems and evaluating the reliability of the resulting Peters-based constraints. This framework offers a computationally inexpensive first step toward reconstructing hierarchical-merger progenitors and provides a foundation for extensions incorporating more sophisticated relativistic treatments.

papers.title: LHAASO Constraints on New-Source Cosmic Rays:Abundance Scenarios and Injection Spectral Indices
papers.abstract: Recent LHAASO observations indicate that microquasars and massive star clusters contribute to Galactic cosmic rays, and likely also to the pre-knee spectral hardening. Their markedly different astrophysical environments, compared with supernova remnants (SNRs), may imprint distinct cosmic-ray abundances. We investigate the spectra and composition of new-source cosmic rays under two abundance scenarios: Case-1, the SNR-like composition with enhanced heavy nuclei, and Case-2, the surface abundances of microquasar companion stars. We constrain injection spectral indices using LHAASO proton, helium, and all-particle spectra, and use their <lnA> data for model discrimination. Under the assumption of a unified heavy-element injection spectrum, Case-2 fits the <lnA> data significantly better than Case-1, but at the cost of large, physically unmotivated differences between heavy-element and He injection indices. This suggests the need to either relax the unified heavy-element injection-index assumption or explore alternative abundance patterns. We predict that if the new-source composition follows Case-1, the individual elemental spectral indices before the knee should remain nearly consistent; if it follows Case-2, the Mg, Si, and Fe spectra will be significantly softer than those of He, C, and O. Future element-resolved energy-spectrum measurements by HERD and LHAASO will provide a decisive test of this discriminating feature.

papers.title: A Very Rich Bimodal Galaxy Cluster Merger: RXC J0032.1+1808
papers.abstract: The galaxy cluster RXC J0032.1+1808 has been well-studied with optical imaging and gravitational lensing mass maps, both of which reveal an elongated morphology in the north-south direction. We find that its X-ray morphology is bimodal, suggesting that it is in the process of merging; combined with a previously reported detection of a radio relic, we suggest that the system is seen after first pericenter. We extract the global X-ray temperature and unabsorbed luminosity from archival XMM-Newton data, finding $T_X=8.5^{+1.1}_{-0.9}$ keV and $L_X=1.04 \pm 0.03 \times 10^{45}$ erg s$^{-1}$ at 90% confidence in the 0.5-10 keV energy range. We conduct a redshift survey of member galaxies and find that the line-of-sight relative velocity between the two subclusters is 1002-1785 km/s at 68% confidence, although the BCGs have an even larger difference of 2466 km/s. We use publicly available hydrodynamic simulations to show that it cannot be a head-on merger; it is consistent with an impact parameter of 0.5 or 1 Mpc. We also use the simulation set to find initial constraints on the time since pericenter (${\approx}$315-550 Myr) and the locus of possible lines of sight.

papers.title: Dirac Observables for Gowdy Cosmologies Regular at the Big Bang
papers.abstract: Gowdy cosmologies are exact, spatially inhomogeneous solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations which describe nonlinear gravitational waves coalescing at the big bang singularity. With toroidal spatial sections they provenly have the asymptotic velocity domination property, in that close to the big bang dynamical spatial gradients fade out and the dynamics is governed by a Carroll-type gravity theory. Here we construct an infinite set of exact Dirac observables for Gowdy cosmologies, valid off-shell, strongly, and without gauge fixing. These observables stay regular at the big bang and can be matched to much simpler Dirac observables of the Carroll-type gravity theory. Conversely, in an adapted foliation there is a systematic anti-Newtonian expansion (in inverse powers of the reduced Newton constant) of the full Dirac observables whose leading terms are the Carroll ones. In particular, this provides an off-shell generalization of the asymptotic velocity domination property.

papers.title: Collider Probes of Dark Energy Microphysics
papers.abstract: The physical origin of dark energy remains one of the most profound open questions in modern physics. Although cosmological observations tightly constrain the equation of state parameter $w$, this information alone does not reveal the underlying microphysics, as many distinct theoretical models can reproduce the same expansion history. A key discriminator among these models is the sound speed of dark energy perturbations, yet this quantity remains largely unconstrained by current astrophysical observations. In this work, we propose a fundamentally new approach: using collider measurements of beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) mediator resonances as a probe of dark energy microphysics. We construct a unified effective-field-theory framework in which a dynamical dark energy scalar is coupled, through symmetry-motivated derivative interactions, to a pseudoscalar mediator in the 2HDM+$a$ model. These interactions naturally induce invisible decays and modify the propagation of the BSM mediator in a dark energy background, leading to measurable distortions of resonance properties at colliders such as the LHC. We show that the decay widths, branching ratios, and kinematic structure of the mediator resonance become sensitive to the propagation properties of dark energy fluctuations, in particular the sound speed. As a result, collider observables provide a direct and complementary handle on dark energy microphysics, with the potential to distinguish between models that are otherwise indistinguishable through cosmology alone. Our results establish a new paradigm in which high-energy collider experiments can probe the physics of cosmic acceleration, revealing a connection between the smallest and largest scales in nature and opening a novel experimental pathway to uncover the fundamental origin of dark energy.

papers.title: Impact of the Einstein Telescope's duty cycle on the estimation of binary black holes parameters
papers.abstract: The geometry of the Einstein Telescope, the proposed next-generation European gravitational-wave observatory, is yet to be finalized. Two competing designs are under consideration: a nested triangular configuration (ET-Δ) and two separated L-shaped detectors (ET-2L). Extensive prior comparisons of ET designs established the scientific landscape using the Fisher-information-matrix formalism and identified that duty-cycle-induced single-detector operation is precisely the regime where this approximation becomes less reliable, underscoring the need for a refined, principled treatment of the duty cycle. In this manuscript, we build on that foundation by revisiting the comparison with full Bayesian parameter estimation of gravitational-wave signals from binary black-hole mergers, projected onto a simulated Einstein Telescope that incorporates a refined duty cycle modelled via continuous-time Markov chains and testing different detector maintenance strategies. We find that the redundancy inherent in the ET-Δ design enables it to maintain at least two operational detectors for the majority of the observing time, whereas the ET-2L configuration is often limited to a single detector. Crucially, we show that, during partial network operation, ET-Δ often outperforms ET-2L, and that the increased multi-detector uptime translates into tighter constraints on the luminosity distance and source-frame component masses. Notably, this remains true even when gravitational-wave events have a lower signal-to-noise ratio in ET-Δ than in ET-2L.

papers.title: Search for Compact Binary Coalescences with Sub-solar Mass Components in Data from the Second Part of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's Fourth Observing Run
papers.abstract: We report on a gravitational wave search for compact binary coalescences with secondary mass between 0.2 M and 1 M and primary mass between 0.2 M and 10 M, restricting the component mass ratio to lie between 0.1 and 1. The analysis uses data collected by the LIGO and Virgo detectors between 2024 April 10 15:00:00 and 2025 January 28 17:00:00, the second part of the fourth observing run of the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration. Results from two out of three search pipelines show outlier candidates, but not at a sufficient level of significance to provide evidence for detection. We report the combined sensitivity of the current searches over the first and second parts of the observing run to the target sub-solar mass (SSM) black hole (BH) population, as well as to neutron star (NS) binaries with one or more sub-solar component. We place upper limits on the merger rate of SSM BHs, ranging from $50 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ to~$5000 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$ (90% confidence) for different component mass combinations. We use the merger rate limits to constrain two illustrative dark matter (DM) scenarios that can form SSM compact objects: primordial BHs, and dark BHs forming in a dissipative DM model. Our search limits the fraction of DM in primordial BHs, assuming a monochromatic mass distribution, to be $\leq$ (0.018-0.032) at 1 M, and $\leq$ (0.10-0.18) at 0.35 M for early-forming binaries; or to be less than 1 at masses above (0.62-0.74) M for late-forming binaries. For the dissipative model, we constrain the fraction of DM for a range of minimum dark black hole masses below $1\,M$ to be as low as (1.0-1.1) x $10^{-5}$; we also exclude minimum masses above (0.62-0.74) M, if dark BHs constitute all of the DM. For binary NSs that include sub-solar mass components, assuming a simple, fixed population model we find a merger rate upper limit of $249 {\rm Gpc}^{-3} {\rm yr}^{-1}$.
authors: J. F. J. van den Brand

papers.title: Exact map-space beam convolution via spin-mapmaking
papers.abstract: Forthcoming cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiments are targeting ambitious science goals, including the exploration of the particle content of the Universe across cosmic times and the search for the faint signal from primordial gravitational waves. To pursue these goals, CMB experiments will house an unprecedented high number of detectors that will dramatically enhance their sensitivity. This will in turn require a tight control of instrumental systematics, demanding efficient and precise simulation of systematic effects. Leveraging spin-mapmaking, we present a map-based method to propagate beam convolution systematics to the map-level, especially well-suited for main-beam studies. From the scanning strategy information compressed into precomputed h-maps and the beam and sky harmonic coefficients, our method directly outputs beam convolved maps. We validate against pixel-centered TOD-level 4π convolution for circular, elliptical, and Planck HFI scanning beams, demonstrating that our method retains agreement to numerical precision, while operating in map space. This formalism enables efficient simulation of beam convolution systematics across the full focal plane of upcoming experiments. As a first practical application, we demonstrate the ability to efficiently produce beam-convolved simulated Planck maps, showing excellent agreement with the QuickPol pipeline at the power-spectrum level. We release a public code, Smarties4Planck, to easily generate such maps for broader use.

papers.title: Evolving dark energy and a younger Universe from cosmic inhomogeneity
papers.abstract: Joint analyses of baryon acoustic oscillations, type Ia supernovae and the cosmic microwave background show a preference for an evolving dark-energy equation of state, and recent studies suggest that cosmic inhomogeneities can produce an apparent evolution of dark energy within general relativity. Here we examine this effect within a framework in which the possibility that matter can be unevenly distributed enters the expansion dynamics directly. The framework yields redshift-dependent effective values of the Hubble constant and of the dark-energy density parameter without introducing a new free parameter. Using CMB-inferred parameters to fix the homogeneous limit, we find that the dark-energy density parameter increases by about eight percent toward the present, from 0.679 to 0.735, while the inferred Hubble constant shifts from the Planck value toward the range obtained from local measurements. Both trends are broadly consistent with published estimates from supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, X-ray clusters and gravitational waves, although a joint analysis of the underlying data is left for future work. Integrating the resulting expansion history gives a present-day cosmic age of 13.521 Gyr, compared with 13.827 Gyr for the homogeneous model; we interpret the difference of 0.306 Gyr as a global time dilation between the two descriptions. The framework also yields the homogeneous-limit dark-energy density parameter, two thirds, from the formation of volume alone. The predicted redshift dependences can be tested against forthcoming measurements of cosmic distances and expansion rates.

papers.title: Quantum noise and torque correlations in a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations entering through weakly transmitting mirrors can limit a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter for low-frequency gravitational-wave detection, even when its optical layout suppresses radiation-pressure back action. We show that, in the Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS), vacuum fields entering from behind the end and middle test masses can dominate the low-frequency quantum noise despite cancellation of the torques on opposite ends of each bar. For a reference configuration with mirror power transmissions of only $10^{-7}$, these fields contribute $89.7\%$ of the total quantum-noise power spectral density at 0.1 Hz. Omitting them would underestimate the amplitude spectral density by a factor of 3.11. Our input-output model connects the correlations produced by successive optical interactions to the forces on each bar and the measured signal. This connection shows why strong torque cancellation does not, by itself, ensure a corresponding improvement in detector sensitivity. Replacing mirror transmission with absorption at fixed reflectivity leaves the excess quantum noise essentially unchanged for the two operating points studied. The predicted signal response and quantum noise agree with independent FINESSE 3 calculations as recycling detuning and homodyne angle are varied. These results establish rear vacuum fields as a limiting noise source in this torsion-bar speed meter and provide quantitative requirements for its mirror and readout design.

papers.title: Coherent Release Fronts in Krylov Chains and Thermal AdS$_2$ Response
papers.abstract: We study coherent release from a finite serial Krylov sector into an exact conformal tail with asymptotically linear Lanczos coefficients. We derive the cumulative occupation up to a cut that moves to greater Krylov depth with time, tracking the probability accumulated behind the propagating front. This quantity separates the release dynamics of the finite sector from subsequent propagation through the tail. The tail sets the logarithmic transit scale, while the finite sector shapes the resulting distribution. The early edge records the number of serial steps before emission, while the late edge reflects slow resonances and interference and can also exhibit logarithmic enhancements. Thus, one- and two-site sectors can share the same leading resonance in their continued-fraction descriptions yet produce distinct cumulative occupation patterns. We illustrate this framework in thermal AdS$_2$, where a dressed oscillator yields, in the weak-coupling limit, a two-site shallow sector coupled to the conformal tail.

papers.title: Black Hole Binary Mergers in Galactic Nuclei: Combined Effects of Secular Dynamics and Stellar Flybys
papers.abstract: Galactic nuclei, with the central supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and surrounding dense star clusters, serve as natural laboratories for studying gravitational dynamics in extreme gravitational environments. In this work, we model the long term evolution of black hole binaries (BHBs) in these environments by incorporating the tidal influence of the central SMBH, the potential of the nuclear star cluster, SMBH induced relativistic precession, and stochastic perturbations from stellar flybys. Our numerical simulations show that the long term evolution of BHBs is predominantly governed by the SMBH-driven ZLK mechanism. However, once stellar flybys are included, they can modify both the binary angular momentum and energy. The cumulative effect of repeated flyby encounters substantially reshapes the long term dynamical evolution, eventually leading systems toward either merger or disruption. Based on a population synthesis study, we find that this combined secular and non-secular channel produces a merger rate of approximately $\mathcal{R}\simeq16\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$, which is significantly higher than the rates predicted by dynamical channels that neglect stellar flybys. Furthermore, we predict that a non-negligible fraction of merging systems would retain detectable eccentricities at low frequencies around 5 Hz, thus providing a distinctive observational signature for next generation ground based GW detectors. Our results demonstrate that the stochastic perturbations from the surrounding environment are essential for modeling BHB evolution in galactic nuclei, and that this channel may contribute a major fraction of observed mergers.

papers.title: specwizard: A Public Python Framework for Creating Synthetic Absorption Spectra from Hydrodynamical Simulations
papers.abstract: We present specwizard, a publicly available modular Python package for generating synthetic absorption spectra from hydrodynamical simulations. The code combines atomic data from the National Institute of Standards and Technology database with ionisation fractions computed using the cloudy spectral synthesis code for multiple ionising backgrounds, enabling consistent modelling of bound--bound and bound--free absorption for resonant transitions of all ions. specwizard employs a column-density--conserving projection scheme, includes natural line broadening for the Lyman series, and offers optional treatments of instrumental resolution and noise for direct comparison with high-resolution quasar spectra. As example applications of the code, we shoot sightlines through the eagle cosmological simulation to generate a z = 3.2 synthetic quasar spectrum containing H i Lyman-series transitions, including damping wings and Lyman-limit absorption. Additionally, we compute metal-absorption lines probing the circumgalactic medium of simulated galaxies, and investigate the correlated absorption of H i and Si iii. We demonstrate that specwizard applied to outputs from eagle accurately reproduces key observational diagnostics of the Lyman-alpha forest, including the redshift evolution of the mean transmission, the transmission PDF and the transmission power spectrum. We take advantage of the fact that the eagle simulation also reproduces the measured evolution of the temperature-density relation to infer the evolution of the amplitude of the ionizing background, finding excellent agreement with recent theoretical models and measurements.

papers.title: CHRONOS Science Program
papers.abstract: Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion-bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS) is a proposed cryogenic torsion-bar interferometer for precision measurements in the 0.1-10 Hz band. A Sagnac speed-meter readout, power and signal recycling, and balanced homodyne detection provide control of the optical response and quantum measurement correlations. This White Paper describes the science program, detector design, calibration, and staged experimental development. The reference sensitivity uses a multi-input quantum model, including rear-mirror vacuum fields and measurement-back-action correlations, combined with classical noise. Two operating points are optimized for complementary power-law-integrated sensitivity objectives. Gravitational-wave forecasts use this common noise budget and state their source and observing assumptions. The program includes intermediate-mass black-hole binaries, stochastic backgrounds, quantum measurement, and terrestrial gravity perturbations. Dark-matter applications are discussed as response and feasibility studies. A differential gravitational calibrator provides a proposed Yukawa-gravity test whose systematic floor is improved by subtracting auxiliary harmonics. These are conditional projections: experimental reach requires validation of the noise, transfer functions, environmental backgrounds, and systematic uncertainties described here.

papers.title: Microcaustics: Fast GPU-Accelerated Dynamical Microlensing of Time-Dependent Extended Sources
papers.abstract: Gravitational microlensing probes unresolved quasar accretion disc structure and compact objects in lens galaxies and is an important systematic in strong-lens time-delay cosmography. Most analyses use static microlensing map simulations because evolving individual microlenses and caustics is computationally prohibitive. We present Microcaustics, a GPU-accelerated Python package built on PyTorch for dynamical microlensing of time-dependent extended sources in strong gravitational lenses. It combines a local-exact/far-field deflection solver, source-directed lens-plane scouting with temporal reuse, and biquadratic inverse polygon mapping (IPM). GPU batching and fused Triton rasterization accelerate the calculation, while binary caustic labels track source-centred crossings. Across three simulated quadruply lensed quasar systems, our package generates a 10-year, 147-frame multiband light curve in an amortized median of 0.68 s (0.88 s with labels) on a consumer GPU with a median light-curve RMSE of 0.35 mmag, while recovering every reference source-centred caustic crossing. At comparable map accuracy, the batched throughput is 780 times higher than that of a recent CUDA IPM implementation and extrapolates to a speedup of millions relative to classic GPU-D. We demonstrate that our IPM converges as $N_{\rm ray}^{-0.84}$, approaching the idealized $N_{\rm ray}^{-1}$ convergence rate of piecewise-affine IPM and improving upon the $N_{\rm ray}^{-1/2}$ inverse ray-shooting rate. We also introduce a GPU-resident general relativistic and reverberating quasar source model and demonstrate our method with an evolving supernova source. These advances make fully dynamical stellar fields practical for Bayesian and simulation-based inference.

papers.title: A catalog of long, eccentric and precessing binary black hole simulations from ICTS-TIFR
papers.abstract: We present a catalogue of 31 binary black hole simulations performed with the Spectral Einstein Code (SpEC) on the Sonic cluster at ICTS-TIFR, Bengaluru between August 2023 and December 2024, targeting the sparsely covered corner of parameter space in which orbital eccentricity and spin-orbit precession are present simultaneously: 17 configurations are both eccentric and precessing, spanning mass ratios $1 \le q \le 11$ and initial eccentricities up to $\hat{e}_0 = 0.40$. The longest, EccPrecDiff002, inspirals for 80 orbits (159 gravitational-wave cycles), to our knowledge the longest simultaneously eccentric and precessing binary black hole evolution to date. Compile-time optimisation of SpEC and its third-party library stack for the AMD Zen-2 architecture delivered a 90% speedup of the initial-data solver and a 40% speedup of the evolution, roughly half of the latter traceable to a single defect in how pre-2.34 glibc reported cache topology on AMD processors. The campaign consumed $1.18 \times 10^{6}$ CPU-hours. We document the post-processing pipeline and validate the frame transformation and waveforms. Eccentricity is measured from the waveforms and compared against the initial data. The first law of binary black hole mechanics, a test of approximate helical symmetry, is satisfied to better than 0.54% for every configuration with $e_ω < 0.2$, and we show that even precessing systems can be regarded as possessing approximate helical symmetry in the co-precessing frame. Using the aligned-spin simulations to calibrate the numerical floor, the co-precessing approximation's mirror-symmetry violation lies three to four ordersof magnitude above it, growing from 0.7% to 5.3%with opening angle. EccPrecDiff002 spans the band above 5 Hz without hybridisationfor $M \le 62\,M_\odot$, giving a single-interferometer signal-to-noise ratio of 961 in Cosmic Explorer at 1 Gpc.

papers.title: Transients and Stellar Activity as Revealed by Ultraviolet Diagnostic Tracers
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) observations offer unique insights into transient and variable astrophysical phenomena, from the Sun and nearby stars to supernovae and star-forming galaxies. Here, we summarise and review the diagnostic power of the UV spectrum for probing the physical conditions, dynamics and energetics of these events. We trace the historical development of UV astronomy from early satellite missions to the current landscape shaped by the Hubble Space Telescope, the GALaxy Evolution eXplorer, the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and AstroSat/UVIT. Particular emphasis is placed on resonance lines such as Mg II $h$ and $k$, C II, Si IV, C IV and N V, which probe the (solar and) stellar chromosphere and transition region, revealing magnetic heating, shocks and mass loss across stellar types. We examine UV diagnostics of stellar flares, pre-main-sequence activity and rotation--activity correlations, linking them to exoplanetary irradiation and habitability. We then explore the UV view of supernova shock breakout and early-time emission, as well as the far-UV mapping of young stellar populations and hierarchical star formation in the Magellanic Clouds. Together, these aspects illustrate how the UV connects small-scale plasma processes to galactic-scale star formation. Despite remarkable progress, UV transient astronomy remains limited by instrument availability and cadence. Forthcoming missions promise to transform this field by capturing the rapid, luminous phenomena that define the dynamic Universe.

papers.title: Hyperaccreting Magnetised Neutron Stars inside Rotating Massive Envelopes: Low-Power Jets and Precursor Flares
papers.abstract: The engulfment of a neutron star (NS) by a massive companion initiates a highly dynamic common-envelope (CE) evolution phase. As the NS spirals into the dense stellar core, it is subjected to hypercritical accretion rates that threaten to rapidly collapse the NS into a black hole (BH). However, if the infalling envelope possesses sufficient angular momentum and magnetic fields, the NS might survive longer and launch feedback-driving jets. To investigate this, we perform fully coupled, axisymmetric General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of hyperaccreting NSs, featuring energy-integrated two-moment neutrino transport and a 13-isotope nuclear reaction network. We systematically vary the envelope rotation profile and the magnetic field strength of the NS surface ($B_{\rm surf} \sim 5 \times 10^{10} - 5 \times 10^{13}$~G). In non-magnetised models, we find that envelope rotation naturally forms a centrifugal barrier and a geometrically thick accretion disk, which suppresses the mass accretion rate and lowers the neutrino luminosity; conversely, the intrinsic spin of the NS has a negligible global impact. In magnetised models, the differential rotation of the accretion flow vigorously amplifies the toroidal magnetic field via the $Ω$-effect, driving the expansion of magnetic towers. Crucially, for strong initial surface magnetic fields ($B_{\rm surf} \gtrsim 2.3 \times 10^{13}$~G), the intense magnetic pressure could completely halt the accretion flow at the NS surface and evacuates a low-density polar funnel. We conclude that while this highly magnetised NS engine successfully delays prompt BH formation and may launch low-power precursor jets (with powers up to ${\sim} 10^{46}~{\rm erg/s}$) capable of generating observable X-ray flares, it lacks the energy budget to unbind the massive envelope, potentially setting the stage for a subsequent BH-driven explosion.

papers.title: Infrared-Finite Positivity Bounds in 4D Gravity
papers.abstract: We formulate an S-matrix bootstrap in an exactly flat half-space, where boundary reflection provides geometric infrared control for four-dimensional gravity. Under the channel positivity conditions, we obtain an infrared-finite positivity bound on local four-scalar Wilson coefficients that includes a finite gravitational correction of order $G_N$ and is derived from the full UV absorptive spectrum without specifying a UV theory, imposing a spectral ansatz, requiring weak coupling or expanding the spectrum perturbatively. At fixed dimensionless external state parameters, the coefficient of the leading gravitational correction is independent of the EFT scale and requires neither an arbitrary soft resolution scale nor a model-dependent UV scale. Gaussian wave-packet scattering localizes interactions within the flat region and directly probes bulk Wilson coefficients while exponentially suppressing sensitivity to the boundary. Long-range gravitons remain sensitive to the boundary and give a finite contribution. The smearing functional passes numerical positivity tests with general half-space absorptive kernels in both crossed channels. An explicit string example shows how boundary reflection suppresses the collective contribution of string resonances to the absorptive part of the amplitude, connecting infrared control of low-energy scattering to the UV spectrum of quantum gravity in the same dispersion relation. The framework opens a route to infrared-finite constraints on effective interactions across particle physics and gravity.

papers.title: Separation of gravitational perturbations of singly spinning Myers-Perry black holes
papers.abstract: Gravitational perturbations of rotating black holes in higher dimensions generally obey coupled partial differential equations. We show that scalar gravitational perturbations invariant under rotations of the transverse sphere of a singly spinning Myers-Perry black hole separate, despite the obstruction to a decoupled Teukolsky equation. Two commuting, second-order angular operators organise the three gauge-invariant curvature components into joint eigenfunctions. The physical radial problem is a $2\times2$ first-order system, equivalent to a single second-order equation. This gives a separation of the sector containing both the bar-mode and axisymmetric ultraspinning instabilities. Using only ordinary differential equations, we compute the bar-mode quasinormal spectrum in $d=5,6,7$ and find instability onsets at $a/r_+=0.90498$ and $0.83228$ in $d=6,7$. We also compute the growing axisymmetric modes and their onset rotations in $d=6,\ldots,9$. The construction shows how separability can survive the coupling between gravitational polarisations.

papers.title: Testing compact binary nature in eccentric orbits with third-generation detectors
papers.abstract: The spin-induced quadrupole moment (SIQM) of a compact object provides a direct null test of the Kerr hypothesis. Most existing gravitational-wave tests of SIQM assume quasi-circular binaries, although dynamical formation channels can produce measurable eccentricity that may persist in the sensitive band of third-generation (3G) detectors. We extend the symmetric SIQM test to eccentric, aligned-spin binaries using a post-Newtonian spinning-eccentric phasing model, and forecast its measurability with Cosmic Explorer (CE) and Einstein Telescope (ET). Single-event Fisher-matrix forecasts show that the impact of eccentricity on SIQM measurement precision depends on the binary parameters and detector configuration, rather than uniformly degrading the measurement. A population study with a truncated eccentric expansion indicates that ET's additional low-frequency eccentric cycles tighten $Δκ_s$ by roughly a factor of two relative to CE (median $0.11$ to $0.12$ versus $0.20$ to $0.23$); the absolute values are indicative only. We further show that quasi-circular template banks can lose significant effectualness for moderately eccentric signals, motivating the development of eccentric-spin template families. Accounting for eccentricity is therefore important both for SIQM measurements and for avoiding systematic losses in searches, and it strengthens tests of the nature of compact objects with 3G gravitational-wave detectors.

papers.title: Collective Properties of Gravitational Perturbations in Thermal Environments on a Dynamical Background
papers.abstract: A thermal plasma dresses soft gauge fields, turning them into collective modes with a plasmon gap and Landau damping. In this paper, we ask whether a thermal radiation plasma does the same to gravitational perturbations. For gravity, the thermal soft scale coincides with the Hubble rate. Any such gap therefore lies at the horizon scale, where the expansion of the background cannot be neglected. We model radiation by a conformal scalar and compute its linear response to metric perturbations directly on a flat FLRW background. We test this response against the diffeomorphism Ward identities. The adiabatic dispersion relation yields a gapped collective mode with $ω_p^2 = 8\mathcal{H}^2/5$, where $\mathcal{H}$ is the conformal Hubble rate. The imaginary part of its frequency, however, is dominated by the background expansion and does not represent Landau damping. In the radiation background, the tensor modes obey a real-time integro-differential equation that reproduces Weinberg's damping of gravitational waves. The initial-time boundary of the retarded response keeps superhorizon modes frozen until horizon reentry despite the gap. The superhorizon growth found in earlier analyses arises from discarding the memory of the retarded response and from a local-equilibrium state prescription that violates the Ward identities. More generally, the Ward identities forbid any local state response beyond the collisionless kernel.

papers.title: Binary Black Hole Coalescence and the Dynamics of Scalar Hair in Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar Theory
papers.abstract: We investigate the head-on coalescence of charged binary black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar (EMS) theory using numerical relativity. The binaries are built from charged puncture initial data representing two Reissner-Nordström black holes immersed in a purely kinetic scalar perturbation: the scalar field initially vanishes, while its conjugate momentum provides a small seed for the instability. We evolve the coupled gravitational, electromagnetic, and scalar sectors and monitor the apparent horizons, the emitted radiation, and the scalar field on the horizons. Our simulations show that the nonminimal electromagnetic-scalar coupling can dynamically trigger the growth of scalar hair even when the individual black holes are initially scalar-free. The subsequent evolution depends on the coupling parameter $α_0$ and on the charge-to-mass ratio of the remnant. For weak coupling, or when charge cancellation suppresses the electromagnetic source after the merger, the scalar field is radiated away or absorbed by the final horizon, and the system dynamically descalarizes. For sufficiently strong coupling and nonzero remnant charge, the scalar field remains finite, and the final black hole approaches a scalarized configuration. For binaries with equal charge-to-mass ratios, $q_1=q_2=0.1$, our simulations identify a transition region between $1900<α_0<2000$, that separates descalarized and scalarized remnants. The coalescence also excites scalar radiation whose time profile is qualitatively correlated with the dominant gravitational-wave mode during the nonlinear stage of the collision. These results provide a binary realization of scalarization/descalarization transitions in EMS theory and show that the fate of scalar hair is controlled by the interplay between the scalar coupling and the charge content of the remnant.

papers.title: Linear Response to Black Hole Deformations
papers.abstract: Modifications of gravity beyond (vacuum) General Relativity have a subtle impact on the physics around black holes. Describing these effects across different observables is, however, a priori strongly model dependent. While effective descriptions of the geometry allow to efficiently capture deviations from benchmark predictions, they sometimes lack a clear passage towards (effective) new physics. Inspired by linear response theory, in this work I therefore propose a formalism that allows to calculate leading corrections of observables relative to the Schwarzschild black hole anywhere in space-time (outside of the horizon): the order of corrections is fixed through an eigenvalue $\mathcal{E}$ of the Einstein tensor, which is identified with an external energy momentum tensor that generates the deformation of the geometry. In this ways, $\mathcal{E}$ can be linked to effective physics models. Focusing on spherically symmetric and static black holes, I illustrate the approach at the hand of a number of observables in the vicinity of the horizon, such as characteristic quantities of particles moving around the black hole (e.g. the black hole shadow or the radius of the innermost stable circular orbit) or the spectrum of scalar quasi-normal modes. Reversing the logic, I argue that the knowledge of such observables provides non-trivial constraints on $\mathcal{E}$, which in turn grant insights into the effective physics in the vicinity of the black hole.

papers.title: MAXI J1820+070: A rapidly spinning black hole with a small disk truncation in the soft state and warm corona layers
papers.abstract: Our study seeks to address the debate over the spin of MAXI J1820+070 through broadband spectral modeling of NICER/NuSTAR observations obtained during the soft state. We further compare our results with previous spin estimates and examine the source variability across the soft state. In addition, we investigate the origin of the soft X-ray excess, which we argue does not originate from the plunging region as previously suggested. To further investigate the origin of this excess, we calculate spin-dependent radial disk temperature profiles across all epochs. We show that the soft spectral state of MAXI J1820+070 is well-described by the Comptonized emission from a thin relativistic accretion disk and two blackbody spectral components with kT$_{bb} = 0.5$ keV and kT$_{bb} = 0.2$ keV. Our results indicate that the black hole in MAXI J1820+070 is rapidly spinning, with $a$ > 0.8, potentially powering the relativistic jets. Our analysis reveals a significant decline in the inner disk temperature midway through the soft state, accompanied by a modest increase in the inferred inner disk radius up to 3Rg. This behavior is consistent with a small disk truncation, a phenomenon recently predicted by GRMHD simulations of the plunging region. The two blackbody components are considerably cooler than the inner disk, corresponding to large emission regions. This suggests that this emission may originate from warm corona layers located further away from the black hole, in close analogy to the warm Comptonization models proposed to explain the soft X-ray excess in active galactic nuclei.

papers.title: Enhancing dark siren cosmology via Gaussian process reconstruction of incomplete galaxy catalogs
papers.abstract: We present a novel framework for improving dark siren cosmology by applying a Gaussian process (GP) to the line-of-sight (LOS) reconstruction of incomplete galaxy catalogs. In the standard galaxy catalog method for inferring the Hubble constant $H_0$ from gravitational-wave (GW) dark sirens, missing galaxies are typically assumed to follow a uniform distribution in comoving volume, an assumption that discards galaxy redshift clustering information crucial for cosmological inference. We propose instead to model the LOS galaxy redshift distribution as a non-parametric function drawn from a GP realization, which is fitted to the observed incomplete catalog via a hierarchical Bayesian likelihood that explicitly accounts for the survey selection function. Applied to mock GW and galaxy catalogs extending up to redshift $z\leq0.4$, our method yields $H_0$ constraints that are on average 23% more precise than the standard homogeneous completion when using a 24%-complete galaxy catalog, and 37% more precise for an 8%-complete catalog. The largest improvement, reaching 66%, is obtained in configurations where the GP most effectively reconstructs the redshift over- and under-density features that the homogeneous completion fails to capture.

papers.title: Cosmological Consequences of a Highly Decoupled Right-handed Neutrino
papers.abstract: In the minimal type-I seesaw, one right-handed neutrino (RHN) can decouple from neutrino mass generation. Such a state is usually neglected, yet its feeble couplings make it long-lived, and it can dominate the energy density of the Universe before decaying. We study this in a minimal $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, where the RHNs are produced through $B-L$ gauge interactions, for the cases of a decoupled lightest RHN $N_1$ and a decoupled heaviest RHN $N_3$. The resulting early matter-dominated era dilutes the baryon asymmetry, and for decoupled $N_3$ it also delays the equilibration of the charged-lepton Yukawa interactions, allowing a lighter $N_1$ to generate the asymmetry in the unflavoured regime. Breaking $U(1)_{B-L}$ forms cosmic strings whose gravitational-wave background acquires a spectral break from the early matter-dominated era, with a frequency set by the decoupled RHN mass and the lightest neutrino mass, within reach of future detectors such as SKA, THEIA, LISA, $μ$ARES, DECIGO and ET.

papers.title: Fast Radio Bursts from Monster Shocks and Flares of Inspiraling Binary Neutron Stars: A Kinetic Model for Double Pulsar
papers.abstract: The coalescence of binary neutron star systems offers unprecedented possibilities for multimessenger observations, including the detection of gravitational waves, gamma-ray bursts, kilonovae, and potentially fast radio bursts. For a detailed investigation of the latter, one requires a kinetic plasma model to describe the interacting magnetospheres of the stars. We present a three-dimensional particle-in-cell kinetic simulation of the combined magnetosphere of a binary neutron star in which the two stars physically orbit one another so that the orbital motion itself twists the magnetic loops. We find that the stellar magnetic-field intensity ratio controls the emergence of flares, while the stellar spins set the direction and modulation of the flare. We identify four spatially and dynamically distinct regions of strong electromagnetic energy release: (i) an expanding fast magnetosonic wave that steepens into a monster shock, (ii) a plasma flare being pushed by (iii) an expanding fireball and containing (iv) a reconnecting current sheet. The fast magnetosonic wave is a promising source of coherent radio emission. It is released when orbital motion cuts a closed plasma loop. The electric and magnetic wave amplitudes are similar and reach that of the background magnetic field. Our kinetic treatment yields particle spectra and plasma structures that can be used to assess coherent emission in kinetic-scale simulations. In conclusion, the stellar orbital motion constitutes a driving channel distinct from models with spin-driven magnetospheric twisting.

papers.title: Onset of Chaos and Orbital Instabilities around Rotating Weyl Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate nonlinear photon motion in the vicinity of a rotating black hole (BH) within Weyl conformal gravity (WCG) by employing Poincare sections, Lyapunov exponents, Fast Lyapunov Indicators (FLI), Kolmogorov-Sinai (KS) entropy, and Discrete Indicator of Chaos (DIG) maps. The joint influence of BH spin and higher order curvature corrections, governed by the parameters $ξ$ and $γ$, induces a transition from nearly integrable trajectories to markedly chaotic dynamics in the strong field domain. As $ξ$ and $γ$ increase, the invariant tori are increasingly deformed and eventually break up. Resonance islands and stochastic layers then form, producing large chaotic regions in phase space, especially near the extremal spin regime. Increasing Lyapunov exponents, faster FLI growth, and higher KS entropy provide quantitative measures of the enhanced dynamical instability, the increased sensitivity to initial conditions, and the corresponding rate of information production. DIG maps show shrinking regular regions and expanding chaotic domains around the photon sphere, indicating that conformal gravity corrections destabilize null circular orbits. Taken together, these findings clarify how relativistic frame dragging and higher order curvature terms jointly control photon chaos and point to nonlinear photon dynamics as a potential probe of departures from General Relativity in the strong-gravity regime.

papers.title: Spectrally enhanced gravitational redshift signals in photonic interferometry
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanics and general relativity are remarkably successful, yet their joint predictions remain beyond direct experimental reach. Photonic interferometers operating in a gravitational field offer a promising route to test this regime: gravitational redshift differentiates photon propagation between vertically separated arms, leading to a predicted phase shift and reduction in interference visibility. These effects are minute on laboratory scales, motivating existing proposals to consider large interferometer areas to accumulate them geometrically. Indeed, such schemes typically require kilometre-scale optical paths to produce appreciable interferometric signals. Here, we propose a strategy that replaces geometric accumulation with spectral enhancement by coupling the two interferometer arms to optical scatterers based on ultranarrow atomic transitions. These transitions serve as local spectral references: gravitational redshift changes the photon's detuning from each resonance, producing large differences in reflection amplitude and hence substantial visibility loss and interferometric phase shift already for centimetre-scale height differences. We quantify the experimental requirements and assess the feasibility of implementation with current or near-term technology. Our proposal thus opens a route to tabletop optical tests of the interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity.

papers.title: Looking for non-gaussianity in Pulsar Timing Arrays through the four point correlator
papers.abstract: Pulsar Timing Arrays have recently reported strong evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. In standard analyses, it is modeled through pulsar-dependent Fourier coefficients assumed to follow gaussian statistics, so that the signal is fully characterized by its two-point function. However, if the background arises from a finite population of inspiralling supermassive black hole binaries, non-gaussian features may emerge, making the determination of higher-order correlators essential. In this work, we compute the complete four-point correlator of the stochastic gravitational wave background Fourier coefficients for four arbitrary pulsar positions, identifying it as the leading probe of non-gaussianity. The result separates into a gaussian contribution, proportional to the square of the two-point function, and a genuinely non-gaussian connected component, whose non-trivial angular dependence generalizes the Hellings and Downs correlation to four pulsars. This angular structure depends only on averages of products of antenna pattern functions, and is therefore expected to be independent of the specific physical origin of the background. We further propose to incorporate the four-point correlator into the parameter-estimation pipeline by deriving a marginalized likelihood that perturbatively accounts for non-gaussian effects. Our results provide the theoretical framework to search for non-gaussian features in pulsar timing array data, opening the way to a more complete characterization of gravitational-wave backgrounds.

papers.title: A fluid dual to the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm
papers.abstract: According to the formulation of the charged large $D$ membrane paradigm, an arbitrary dynamic black hole solution to a theory of gravity with a $U(1)$ gauge field is dual to the dynamics of a membrane in a non-gravitational background. This membrane is endowed with a stress-energy tensor and a charge current, whose conservation equations govern its dynamics. In this work, we demonstrate that the dynamics of these membrane configurations (at the leading nontrivial order in $1/D$) can be mapped to a relativistic charged fluid, establishing a correspondence for asymptotically flat black holes with a particular class of fluid systems. Unlike the standard AdS/Hydrodynamics correspondence, this dual fluid does not reside on an asymptotic boundary, but is localised strictly on the non-gravitational membrane worldvolume. By evaluating the system in both the Eckart and Landau frames, we systematically extract the out-of-equilibrium transport coefficients. We find that the fluid is governed by a negative effective thermal conductivity and a negative heat capacity. This mechanism provides a hydrodynamic interpretation of thermodynamic stability, effectively translating the previously established quasinormal mode damping of the large-$D$ Reissner-Nordström geometry into the language of fluid dynamics.

papers.title: Mapping Dark Matter in Merging Clusters with Weak Lensing for CSST: Morphology and Filament Recovery
papers.abstract: Weak gravitational lensing offers a direct probe of the projected dark matter distribution in cluster-scale structures and the surrounding cosmic web. We investigate the capability of the China Space Station Telescope (CSST) to recover non-spherical dark matter morphologies using mock reduced-shear maps generated from cosmological N-body simulations. We apply the deep-learning-based MIU2Net mass-reconstruction framework to CSST-like wide- and deep-field source densities, focusing on two representative systems: filament-connected halo pairs and elongated halos. MIU2Net accurately recovers halo centers, elongated mass distributions, and the filamentary structures connecting halo pairs in both survey configurations. Halo centers are localized within about 0.1 h^(-1) Mpc, and elongated-halo shapes and orientations are reliably recovered. Filament paths are stable against shape noise, with mean normalized instability parameters I_F, defined as the mean deviation from the true filament locus in units of R_200, decreasing from 0.041 to 0.037 in the low-redshift bin and from 0.051 to 0.045 in the high-redshift bin from the wide to deep field. The recovered filament shapes remain consistent with the true maps at the percent level. Compared with conventional Kaiser-Squires reconstruction, MIU2Net better preserves low-contrast anisotropic structures while suppressing small-scale noise. These results demonstrate that CSST weak-lensing data, combined with machine-learning-based mass reconstruction, will enable statistical studies of cluster assembly, anisotropic matter accretion, and the connection between massive halos and the filamentary cosmic web.

papers.title: Black holes with dark matter halos and a positive cosmological constant: Energy conditions and signatures
papers.abstract: We study static, spherically symmetric black holes surrounded by dark matter halos in the presence of a positive cosmological constant. Assuming vanishing radial pressure, we derive the constraints imposed by the null, weak, strong, and dominant energy conditions on the halo matter. The halo is confined to a finite radial interval separated from both horizons, and the total mass is bounded above by the Nariai value. We construct a Hernquist-type profile and study black hole images, showing that a positive cosmological constant can substantially change the images. We also compute scalar quasinormal modes of the Hernquist-type spacetime. When the dark matter mass is sufficiently small, the relative difference of a selected mode is approximately linear in the compactness of the matter halo, i.e., the ratio of mass parameter $M_{\text{DM}}$ and scale parameter $a$, with a coefficient that depends on the cosmological constant.

papers.title: A Horizon-to-Boundary Dictionary Linking Smooth Horizon Continuation, Pole-Skipping, and $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ Lowest-Weight Structure
papers.abstract: We study pole-skipping for a scalar field in the JT/AdS$_2$ black-hole background. Previous work established the local mechanism: at a pole-skipping point, a near-horizon recurrence relation becomes degenerate and an additional regular expansion coefficient is left undetermined. We take this local degeneracy as the starting point and track two independent solutions normalized at the AdS boundary, denoted by $R_1$ and $R_2$ for the source and response branches, respectively. Let $\widehat A$ and $\widehat B$ denote the source and response coefficients after their common singular factor is removed, and let $χ_μ$ denote the universal ingoing horizon factor. We find \[ \widehat A=0 \Longleftrightarrow \frac{R_2}{χ_μ}\in C^\infty, \qquad \widehat B=0 \Longleftrightarrow \frac{R_1}{χ_μ}\in C^\infty . \] Thus the source and response zeros correspond separately to horizon smoothness of the two boundary-normalized solutions after the ingoing factor is removed. At integer resonance the local regular solution contains an additional coefficient $a_N$. In the JT/AdS$_2$ model, continuation of the nonresonant ingoing solution fixes $a_N=0$ and thereby selects a unique retarded value at resonance, although unrestricted approaches in parameter space remain path dependent. At the endpoint of the pole-skipping lattice, the response branch is a lowest-weight state of the background $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry. A static holographic-superconductor example further shows that simultaneous horizon smoothness is insufficient if the two boundary branches are linearly dependent. A two-branch pole-zero intersection therefore requires \[ W[R_1,R_2]\neq0. \] These results distinguish the known local horizon degeneracy from the global relation between boundary branches and the resonant horizon solution space.

papers.title: Mathematical framework for simulation of non-perturbative cavity optomechanics with plate-like dielectrics
papers.abstract: Cavity optomechanical models typically treat a sensor either as a perturbative polarizable object in a pre-existing optical field, or solve the field at a fixed equilibrium and linearize in a fixed optical-mode basis. Neither self-consistently determines the spatially resolved cavity field, the optical force, the mechanical equilibrium, and the back-action when a finite-thickness dielectric plate intercepts the entire optical mode and restructures the intracavity field. In this companion paper to [1], we develop that treatment by extending the vacuum two-photon formalism to finite-thickness planar dielectrics, incorporating their Fresnel reflection, internal propagation, optical forces, and mechanical back-action directly into the field equations. We derive the carrier and sideband transfer functions needed to describe the coupled optical-mechanical system, including optomechanical cooling and the response to external perturbations. The result is a systematic starting point for calculating detector response and noise budgets for cavity experiments with intracavity dielectrics, including gravitational wave detectors deploying levitated sensors.

papers.title: Einstein Telescope: the triangle in a network and the impact of the relative orientation of detectors
papers.abstract: The geometrical configuration of the Einstein Telescope (ET) gravitational-wave observatory is one the most important design choices to be made for this future scientific facility. Two baseline configurations are currently being considered, a single triangle or 2 distant L-shaped detectors tilted by about $45^{\circ}$. In this document we present a study of the scientific performance of the ET baseline configurations in both stand-alone mode and in the presence of either an L-shaped Cosmic Explorer detector with 40-km long arms located in the United States or the existing LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network. We also include in the study an alternative ET configuration, which is currently not being considered and consists of a triangle plus a distant L-shaped detector. We find that in stand-alone mode this alternative configuration performs significantly better than the other two in both the compact binary coalescence and stochastic gravitational wave background scientific cases. The differences in performance between the ET configurations are reduced in the presence of the considered, additional non-ET detectors. We also show that the impact of possible correlated noise in co-located detectors on the stochastic gravitational-wave background performance can be addressed with the addition of extra detectors. Finally, we study the impact on the ET scientific performance of the relative orientation of the future detectors in the network. We find that, while the configurations that include a triangular ET detector are basically insensitive to this orientation, a balanced compromise for the ET configuration consisting of two L-shaped detectors could be represented by a tilt angle between the two detectors of about $30^{\circ}$.

papers.title: Mergers Fall Short: Non-merger Channels Required for Galactic Heavy Element Production
papers.abstract: Since the discovery of the binary neutron star merger GW170817 and its associated kilonova, neutron star mergers have been established as a key production channel for r-process elements in the Universe. However, various lines of evidence, including observations of r-process abundances inferred from stellar spectra of Milky Way disk stars, suggest that additional channels are needed to fully account for r-process element enrichment in the Milky Way. Neutron star-black hole mergers and fast-merging binary neutron star systems are among the leading alternative candidates. In this paper, we combine gravitational-wave observations from LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA with data from short gamma-ray bursts, Galactic pulsars, and Galactic Eu/Fe versus Fe/H abundance observations to assess the contribution of these mergers to r-process enrichment in the Galactic disk. Our analysis employs a unified, likelihood-based inference framework that consistently propagates uncertainties in merger rates, delay-time distributions, mass- and spin-dependent ejecta yields, and stellar abundance measurements. We find that neither neutron star-black hole mergers nor fast- merging binary neutron star populations can serve as the dominant additional channel without generating strong tension with existing observations and theoretical expectations. These results constrain the viable sources of Galactic r-process enrichment and underscore the necessity of non- merger production channels.

papers.title: Physical characteristics of the Galaxy defining the oscillation period of librating orbits near the OLR of the bar
papers.abstract:
We studied librating orbits of stars near the Outer Lindblad Resonance (OLR) of the bar using the angle-action variables of Hamiltonian dynamics. The librating orbits change the direction of their elongation relative to the major axis of the bar in a limited range of angles. To calculate orbits, we used the model of the Galaxy with an analytical bar which reproduces well the distributions of the observed stellar velocities along the Galactocentric distance R derived from the Gaia DR3 data. We compared the values of the orbital oscillation period of a typical star obtained from the theory and with the use of numerical simulation. Both values were found to be in good agreement and are equal to 2.0 Gyr. It was shown that the change in the average orbital radius, , of a star, calculated over the time interval of one radial oscillation, is regulated by the change in the direction of orbital elongation. As the orbit is tilted relative to the minor axis of the bar in the sense of Galactic rotation, the angular momentum of the star, L, decreases, on average, causing a decrease in . papers.title: Innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) of arbitrary-mass compact binaries with spins at the fourth post-Newtonian order
papers.abstract: We compute, up to 4th post-Newtonian (4PN) order, the gauge-invariant stability criterion determining the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) for arbitrary-mass compact binaries with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum. Our calculation, a perturbation analysis, incorporates spin-orbit and spin-spin contributions, both up to next-to-next-to-leading order, as well as leading-order cubic and quartic spin contributions, all calculated in prior works within the effective-field-theory (EFT) Hamiltonian formalism. In the test-mass limit, we recover the Kerr ISCO truncated at 4PN order. Estimating the ISCO shift at first order in the mass ratio and comparing our results with numerical gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations, we find good agreement for retrograde spin (the smallest discrepancy being obtained for maximal retrograde spin) and moderate prograde spin. For nearly maximal prograde spin, the PN approach fails to determine the ISCO, for it is close to the black hole (BH) horizon. We also estimate the ISCO shift due to the test-particle spin and compare our result with the exact prediction from the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon (MPD) equations for a spinning particle orbiting a Kerr black hole. Finally, we discuss the stability and the ISCO of corotating black-hole binaries.

papers.title: Matching Tidal Deformability (Wilson) Coefficients to Black Hole Love Numbers in Higher-Curvature Gravity
papers.abstract: We present a consistent mapping between tidal deformability coefficients (tidal Love numbers) and Wilson coefficients in effective field theory (EFT) descriptions of higher-curvature theories of gravity. In this work, we focus on the connection between the static response of a non-spinning black hole and the corresponding Wilson coefficient governing tidal imprints in gravitational-wave signals. We analyze a set of control cases to identify the key ingredients required for a systematic computation and matching procedure. In doing so, we highlight shortcomings in existing results that rely on the standard matching approach used in General Relativity when applied to higher-curvature gravity theories. As an explicit demonstration, we compute the relevant coefficients for cubic gravity theories. Our findings bridge an important gap in the correspondence between tidal Love numbers and Wilson coefficients in EFT extensions of General Relativity, which had not been thoroughly explored previously.

papers.title: Constants of motion and fundamental frequencies for elliptic orbits at fourth post-Newtonian order: aligned-spin contributions
papers.abstract: For eccentric systems with aligned spins, we compute all spin contributions to the gauge-invariant conservative map between the constants of motion (energy and angular momentum) and the fundamental (radial and azimuthal) frequencies at the fourth post-Newtonian order. This extends the nonspinning map derived in [arXiv:2511.10735] to include terms that are linear, quadratic, cubic, and quartic in spin, as well as the associated spin-deformability parameters. We also obtain derived quantities such as the redshift and gyroscopic invariants, as well as circular links. We notice that the Blanchet-Iyer-Favata post-Newtonian stability criterion that determines the dimensionless frequency of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) is in fact intricately related to the periastron advance for circular orbits. Finally, in the case of unbound orbits, we complete the 4PN scattering angle with all spin contributions.

papers.title: Nonlinear Perturbations of Relativistic Stars
papers.abstract: We extend the general relativistic Lagrangian perturbation formalism of Friedman and Schutz [Astrophys. J. 200, 204 (1975)] beyond linear order, retaining full time dependence of the perturbations. We provide general formulae to relate the Lagrangian and Eulerian perturbations to any general perturbative order. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to tidally perturbed relativistic stars in Regge-Wheeler gauge and reduce the second-order field and conservation equations to master equations with a nonlinear source. Projecting the source onto the star's eigenmodes, we obtain a nonlinear equation of motion for the mode amplitudes and the coupling coefficients, which describe the interactions among the eigenmodes and with the external tidal field. Approximating the tidal field and the coupling coefficients, we compute the static quadratic Love number from the quadrupolar fundamental mode alone and find that it reproduces the direct metric-matching value to a reasonable accuracy of $4\%$, up to a further correction arising from the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of the second-order tidal field.
